f23: Manastorm Spells are powerful abilities that aid you in the Manastorm, with up to four active at a time. They come in eight ranks and can be unlocked or upgraded using Bonzo Bolts at Cogsworth.
f40:
Manastorm Spells are unique, powerful abilities designed to help you navigate and survive the chaos of the Manastorm. These spells offer a wide range of effects such as bonus stats, crowd control, or utility, that can turn the tide of battle or provide crucial support in challenging scenarios.

You can equip up to four spells at a time, known as your 'Active Manastorm Spells'. These spells can be swapped out to suit your playstyle, role, or the specific challenge you're facing. You can view all of your acquired Manastorm Spells in your Spellbook, under the Ascension Manastorm Items tab.

Each spell can upgrade up to eight different ranks. Higher ranks provide significantly more powerful effects, improving damage, healing, stats, or duration, based on the spell type. Upgrading your spells is essential for keeping pace with the increasing difficulty of Manastorm content.

You can use Bonzo Bolts get new spells or upgrade existing ones from Cogsworth.

f23:
Marks of Ascension can be earned from every type of content in the game and are stored in the Currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab). 

Marks can be used to buy ability purges, talent purges, gear, Heirlooms, and Mystic Enchanting items from Nozdormu.
f40:
Marks of Ascension are a Currency earned from virtually every type of content in the game including PvP encounters, finishing a quest, or completing a dungeon or raid. These tokens are stored in your Currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab) and serve as one of the primary ways to progress and refine your character.

Marks of Ascension can be spent at Nozdormu, found in your Capital City, where they can be exchanged for a wide selection of items. These include ability purges, talent purges, and Mystic Enchanting materials which can help you reset or fine-tune your build. You can also buy high-level gear, heirlooms, and other essential tools to enhance your power or level up faster.

f23: Reforging Mystic Scrolls at an Enchanting Altar grants experience towards your realm-wide Mystic Enchanting level, rewarding a Mystic Extract each time you level up.
f40:
Each time you reforge one of your Mystic Scrolls at an Enchanting Altar, you earn Mystic Enchanting Experience. Gaining enough experience will increase your Mystic Enchanting level, which rewards you with a Mystic Extract used to permanently add an enchant to your collection.

You can track your experience progress directly at any Enchanting Altar. Mystic Enchanting levels are realm-wide, meaning all your characters on the same server contribute to and share the same level progression.

f23: Marks of Ascension can be earned from many types of content and are stored in the Currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab). Marks can be spent at key vendors for progression, catch-up items, Heirlooms, gear, and Wildcard services from Silas Darkmoon.
f40: Marks of Ascension are a Currency earned from many types of content including PvP encounters, finishing quests, or completing dungeons and raids. These tokens are stored in your Currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab) and serve as one of the primary ways to progress and refine your character. On Wildcard, Marks of Ascension can be used at Silas Darkmoon for Scrolls of Fortune and Skill Card Packs. Marks can also be spent at other key vendors for gear, Heirlooms, and other progression tools that help you catch up or strengthen your character.

f23:
Enchanting Altars let you obtain, collect, and apply powerful Mystic Enchants to enhance your character.

You can find permanent altars in the open world or use summonable ones, often purchased from the Auction House or Ascension Store, in major cities and quest hubs.
f40:
Enchanting Altars allow you to obtain, collect, and apply thousands of potential Mystic Enchants to achieve your maximum power! 

You can discover altars in the open world by finding an enchanting altar symbol on your World Map. Altars can also be summoned by your fellow players for a short duration, most often in your Capital City and other major quest hubs. 

Summonable enchanting altars can be obtained from the Auction House for gold or purchased from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

f23:
Active mystic enchants are the enchants your character currently has equipped that alter your abilities, stats, and overall playstyle. 

To apply or change your active enchants, you must be at an Enchanting Altar.
f40:
Active Mystic Enchants are the enchants your character currently has equipped that alter your abilities, stats, and overall playstyle. You can view and manage your Active Mystic Enchants at any time by opening the Mystic Enchant menu (Hotkey N -> Mystic Enchant Tab -> Enchant Collection). To apply or change your activeenchants, you must be at an Enchanting Altar, which can be found in the open world or summoned by other players in major cities.

Each character can have up to 17 Mystic Enchants active at once, with specific limits based on enchant rarity. These limits include: 1 legendary and 3 epic quality enchants active simultaneously. Legendary Enchants typically serve as the core of your build, providing transformative effects or new crucial abilities. Rare and Epic Enchants offer complementary bonuses and synergistic effects that enhance or support your overall playstyle.

Some enchants are stackable, meaning you can equip multiple copies of the same enchant. In these cases, you can have up to three versions of the same enchant active simultaneously. However, not all enchants can be stacked, so it's important to check the tooltip in the Mystic Enchant Collection to see if stacking is allowed for a particular enchant.

f23: Realm-Bound items, commonly referred to as Bind-on-Account (BoA) items, are special items with beige text that can be shared across all characters on your account, but only within the same realm.
f40:
Realm-Bound items (commonly referred to as Bind-on-Account or BoA items) are special items appearing with beige text that can be shared across all characters on your account, but only within the same realm.

Realm-Bound items include things like Heirlooms, vanity items, Donation items, and purchases from the Ethereal Bazaar. Most of these items can be stored in your Vanity Collection (Hotkey N -> Vanity Tab). This makes them easy to equip across your characters without having to mail them individually.

If you need to transfer a Realm-Bound item to a different live server, you’ll need to speak to Courier Malik, an NPC who can assist with cross-realm Vanity item transfers. But keep in mind that only items that can be saved in the Vanity Collection qualify for this service.

f23:
Adventure Mode is a trial that transforms all open-world monsters into dangerous Elites.

In this challenging mode, you'll earn less Experience from defeating enemies, but much more from completing quests, encouraging progression through exploration and objectives rather than relying on enemy kills for Experience.
f40:
Adventure mode is a special trial that significantly increases the difficulty of open-world gameplay by turning all monsters into elite enemies. These enemies hit harder, have more health, and require more tactical strategy to overcome.

While defeating monsters in adventure mode grants less Experience, completing a quest rewards significantly more, encouraging players to focus on exploration, objectives, and progression rather than relying on enemy kills to level.

This mode is ideal for those who enjoy a more immersive and rewarding leveling journey, where every encounter is meaningful and every quest completed brings you closer to greatness. 

You can activate this trial by speaking to Stony Tark in your starting zone or Capital City.

To apply or change your active enchants, you must be at an Enchanting Altar.
f40:
Active mystic enchants are the enchants your character currently has equipped that alter your abilities, stats, and overall playstyle. You can view and manage your active enchants at any time by opening the Mystic Enchant menu (Hotkey N -> Mystic Enchant Tab -> Enchant Collection). To apply or change your enchants, you must be at an Enchanting Altar, which can be found in the open world or summoned by other players in major cities.

Each character can have up to 11 mystic enchants active at a time, once the enchanting slot is unlocked through level progression.

Once unlocked, you can use up to 1 legendary, 1 artifact, 3 epic, and 6 rare quality enchants active simultaneously. Legendary Enchants typically serve as the core of your build, providing transformative effects or new crucial abilities. Artifact Enchants provide a utility spell to your kit, which can include movement abilities, defensive spells, or Crowd Control (CC). Rare and Epic Enchants offer complementary bonuses and synergistic effects that enhance or support your overall strategy.

f23: Agility is the Primary Attribute for those who rely on speed, precision, and deadly efficiency. It’s ideal for players who prefer fast-paced combat, weaving together rapid attacks, critical strikes, and nimble movement.
f40:
Agility is the Primary Attribute for those who rely on speed, precision, and deadly efficiency. It’s ideal for players who prefer fast-paced combat, weaving together rapid attacks, critical strikes, and nimble movement. Agility is especially beneficial for leather and mail armor users who favor mobility over brute force or spellcasting.

Choosing the Path of Finesse makes Agility your main stat, enhancing your offensive potential. You gain bonus Agility, and each point further increases your Attack Power, Critical Strike Chance, and Critical Strike Damage, sharpening every strike you land.

The Path of Finesse also provides two powerful passive abilities based on your weapon setup:

Agile Strikes: When wielding a one-handed weapon, your damaging melee and ranged abilities have their global cooldown and energy/mana cost reduced by 8%, allowing for faster, more efficient combat flow.

Fatal Wounds: When using a two-handed weapon, your melee and ranged ability critical strike damage bonus is increased by 20%, turning every critical hit into a devastating blow.

f23:
Alchemy is a Primary Profession and a Crafting Profession that creates potions, elixirs, flasks, and oils.

Alchemy is reliant on Herbalism for materials.
f40:
Alchemy is a Primary Profession and a Crafting Profession for players who want to create powerful consumables that enhance combat performance, provide utility, and support group content. Alchemists craft potions, elixirs, and flasks that can restore health or mana, boost stats, grant resistances, and more.

To begin, you’ll need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn alchemy. Once you've trained the skill, you can start collecting the materials needed to craft your Recipes. Alchemy relies primarily on herbs gathered through Herbalism, though some potions may also require items purchased from Vendors or obtained in the world.

Using crafted potions is as simple as clicking on them in your inventory, but creating them can require access to an alchemy lab. While lower-level potions can be crafted anywhere, some advanced recipes may require special crafting areas, depending on the level of difficulty.

Alchemy does not require a tool for most crafts, but a philosopher’s stone can be needed for some transmutations. For those managing multiple professions, investing in an Ethereal Tool Dispenser can be helpful as this item consolidates all Profession tools into a single inventory slot and is available from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP) or from the Auction House for in-game gold.

f23:
By clicking the (?) in the Micro Menu or visiting Ameer Greatluck in a Capital City, you can access the Recovery Service menu. 

This is a very useful tool to regain items that have been sold to a Vendor, deleted, or disenchanted.
f40:
Ameer Greatluck is a helpful NPC located in all Capital Cities who provides access to the Recovery Services menu which can restore accidentally lost items. You can reach this service by clicking the (?) icon in your Micro Menu or by speaking directly to Ameer.

Through Recovery Services, you can reclaim items that were sold to a Vendor, deleted, or even disenchanted. Whether it’s a rare drop or a piece of important gear, Ameer Greatluck gives you a second chance to recover your lost valuables.

f23: Area: 52 is Ascension's main Classless realm. With Free-Pick Mode, players can customize their heroes by selecting spells and Talents from any class enabling a high degree of personalization and a near-endless opportunity to create the perfect build.
f40:
Area: 52 is Ascension’s main Classless Realm, where players build their heroes by choosing spells and Talents from any of the original vanilla classes. This system offers deep customization and endless build variety, allowing you to craft truly unique playstyles.

Unlike the Seasonal Realm, progress on Area: 52 is permanent. When the Seasonal Realm ends, your characters transfer here along with their gear, enchants, and vanity items, so you can continue your journey without losing your accomplishments.

Area: 52 is home to a massive, active community, making it an ideal place for long-term progression, PvE, PvP, and creative build crafting.

f23: Sub-Zones are named areas within a zone. The first time you discover a Sub-Zone, you’ll earn a small amount of Experience and unveil its unique location on your World Map.
f40:
Sub-Zones are smaller, named areas within a larger zone. The first time you enter a Sub-Zone, you’ll earn a small amount of Experience and unveil its unique location on your World Map, helping you track where you’ve been.

You can hover your mouse over any revealed area on the World Map to see the name of the Sub-Zone. These areas are often tied to quests, gathering materials, and exploration achievements, making them valuable to discover during your journey.

f23: Arena Rating is a score that represents your skill level in rated Arena matches. This system helps to create balanced games in your rated Arenas so you can face off against similarly-rated opponents.
f40:
Arena Rating is a score that reflects your performance and skill level in rated Arena matches. 

Every player begins at a base rating of 0, and your score will increase or decrease depending on the outcome of your matches. Winning a match raises your rating, while losing one reduces it. This system ensures you're paired against opponents of similar skill, making for more balanced and competitive fights.

Each Arena bracket (1v1, 2v2, and 3v3) has its own separate scoring, meaning your performance in one bracket won’t affect your rating in the others. This allows players to specialize in their favorite formats without penalty.

You can view your current Arena Rating by opening the PvP Menu (Hotkey H -> Rated).

Marks can be used to buy Scrolls of Talent Unlearning, gear, Heirlooms, and other convenient tools from Nozdormu in your Capital City.
f40:

These tokens are stored in your Currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab) and serve as one of the primary ways to progress and refine your character.

Marks of Ascension can be spent at Nozdormu, found in your Capital City, where they can be exchanged for a wide selection of items. These include Scrolls of Talent Unlearning, gear, heirlooms, and other convenient tools to enhance your power or level up faster.

f23: An Arena Season is a distinct competitive period where players can participate in Rated Arena matches to increase their Arena Rating. Each Season has unique rewards that are earned by achieving certain scores.
f40:
The Arena Season is a defined competitive period during which players participate in rated Arena matches to climb the Arena Rating ladder. Each season offers a fresh opportunity to compete for exclusive seasonal rewards.

With the start of every season, a new tier of PvP equipment becomes available for purchase from the PvP Quartermaster, using Arena Points. While some of this gear is accessible to all players, the most powerful equipment requires you to achieve a specific Arena Rating before they can be unlocked for purchase.

At the end of the season, ratings reset, rankings are tallied, and top-performing players receive special end-of-season rewards. Once a new season begins, all players start fresh, ready to compete again in a new cycle of progression and prestige.

You can view the current, previous, and upcoming seasons at:

https://ascension.gg/en/timeline

f23:
Arena Points are a Currency earned by participating in Arenas to buy powerful PvP gear from the PvP Vendors. 

There are several tiers of items you can buy, though some must be unlocked by achieving a specific Arena Rating.
f40:
Arena Points are a form of currency earned by participating in rated arenas. They’re primarily used to purchase powerful PvP gear from PvP Quartermasters located in Capital Cities and PvP hubs.

With the start of every Arena Season, a new tier of PvP equipment becomes available for purchase from the PvP Quartermaster using Arena Points. While some of this gear is accessible to all players, the most powerful equipment requires you to achieve a specific Arena Rating before they can be unlocked for purchase.

Arena Points are stored in your Currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab).

f23:
An arena is a fast-paced, instanced PvP battle to the death. Players can fight in 1v1, 2v2, or 3v3 styled teams to test their skills in a casual or competitive clash! 

You can queue for an Arena with the PvP menu (Hotkey H -> Choose Skirmish for a casual arena, or find the Rated tab for a competitive experience)!
f40:
An arena is a fast-paced, instanced PvP battle to the death where players compete in small team-based matches. Designed to test skill, coordination, and build power, Arenas come in three formats: 1v1 duels, 2v2, and 3v3 team fights. Whether you're looking for casual combat or competitive glory, Arena offers something for every PvPer.

You can queue for Arenas through the PvP menu (Hotkey H) by selecting Skirmish for a casual match or heading to the Rated tab to enter ranked competitive play. Rated Arenas award Arena Points, used to purchase powerful PvP gear from a PvP Quartermaster, and affect your Arena Rating, which determines your standing on the leaderboard.

f23:
There are four types of armor: Cloth, Leather, Mail, and Plate. The type of gear you can equip depends on your class. 

Each armor type provides a different amount of Armor, with Cloth providing the least amount of protection and Plate providing the most.
f40:
Armor Type determines the kind of gear your character can equip and how much physical protection it provides. There are four types of equipment: Cloth, Leather, Mail, and Plate.

Different armors offer different levels of Armor rating, which reduces incoming physical damage.

- Cloth offers the least protection but is commonly used by casters for its magical bonuses.
- Leather provides moderate defense and is favored by agile classes.
- Mail offers more hardiness but still some dexterity and is used by archers or armored casters.
- Plate delivers the highest physical resistance and is worn by a melee fighter or a Tank.

The type of equipment you can wear is determined by your class, and you may need to train your proficiencies at a Class Trainer to wear higher-tier types like Mail or Plate.

Choosing the right equipment isn’t just about defense. Each piece of gear often comes with stats tailored for specific roles, like Intellect for casters or Strength for melee builds. Wearing the proper equipment for your role ensures both survivability and performance in combat.

f23: Armor is a defensive stat that reduces the physical damage your character receives. It’s found on most pieces of gear, with its value heavily influenced by the item’s Armor Type.
f40:
Armor is a defensive stat that reduces the physical damage your character receives. It is found on most pieces of gear, and its value is heavily influenced by the item’s Armor Type (such as cloth, leather, mail, or plate).

The higher your armor rating, the less damage you take from physical attacks, making it a key stat for survivability in both PvE and PvP.

You can view your current Armor value in Character Info (Hotkey C).

f23: Armor Penetration (or ARP) is a secondary stat that lets your attacks bypass a portion of your enemy’s armor, increasing the damage of your physical abilities.
f40:
Armor Penetration (or ARP) is a secondary stat that allows your attacks to bypass a portion of your enemy’s armor, increasing the damage of your physical abilities. Since ARP is percentage-based, it is especially effective against heavily armored foes, though it offers less benefit when facing lightly armored targets.

You can view your current penetration rating by mousing over Hit Rating in the Character Info (Hotkey C).

f23: Attack Power (also known as AP) is a secondary stat that increases the damage you deal with physical attacks.
f40:
Attack Power (also known as AP) is a secondary stat that directly increases the damage of your physical attacks and abilities.

You can find your current Attack Power in Character Info (Hotkey C).

f23:
To enter certain Raid or Dungeon instances, you may need to meet specific requirements (typically quests or reputation milestones) known as the attunement process. 

In Ascension, only the current tier of Ascended Raids requires attunement to unlock.
f40:
Attunement refers to the process of meeting specific requirements such as completing quests, reaching certain reputation levels, or progressing through key storylines, in order to gain access to certain Raid or Dungeon instances.

In Ascension, attunement is only required for the current tier of Ascended Raids, ensuring that players are properly prepared for the challenge ahead. Older content and lower difficulty Raids do not require attunement, making it easier to explore past content at your own pace. 

You can check your attunement progress through quest logs, the reputation panel, or by speaking with related NPCs near raid entrances in the open world.

f23:
The Auction House is an in-game marketplace where players buy and sell items using gold, serving as the central hub for all player-to-player transactions. 

The Auction House is located in your Capital City, use the Map Lens to find an Auctioneer or ask a guard for directions.
f40:
The Auction House is the primary in-game marketplace, allowing players to buy and sell items using gold. From gear and crafting materials to vanity equipment and even Donation Items, the Auction House serves as the central hub for all player-to-player transactions.

You can list your own items for sale or browse listings posted by others, making it a powerful tool for both making gold and acquiring rare or useful items. The market is dynamic and prices can fluctuate, so savvy trading can be very rewarding.

Auction Houses are located in every Capital City. Use the Map Lens to locate an Auctioneer on your minimap, or ask a guard for directions.

f23:

Marks can be used to unlearn and reassign Talents, or purchase Talent Purges, gear, and Heirlooms from Nozdormu in your Capital City.
f40:
Marks of Ascension are a versatile Currency earned from virtually every type of content in the game including quests, Dungeons, PvP, Raids, and world events. These tokens are stored in your Currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab) and serve as one of the primary ways to progress and refine your character.

Marks of Ascension are used whenever unlearning and reassigning your Talents. Alternatively, they can also be spent at Nozdormu for a wide selection of items. These include full Talent Purges, gear, Heirlooms, and other convenient tools to enhance your power or level up faster.

f23:
The Ascension Store offers a wide variety of cosmetics, Heirlooms, Bags, and other convenience items, all available for purchase with Donation Points (DP). 

Most store items are tradable and can often be found on the Auction House or from Tiraxis in exchange for in-game currency.
f40:
The Ascension Store offers a wide variety of cosmetics, Heirlooms, Bags, and other convenience items designed to enhance your experience. All items in the store are purchased using Donation Points (DP).

Most store items are tradable, meaning they can be listed on the Auction House or exchanged through Tiraxis for in-game currency, making many store-exclusive items accessible even to non-donating players.

You can access the store through the Ascension launcher or by visiting ascension.gg/store.

Each realm has its own separate store, so availability and purchase history are unique per realm. Be sure to check which realm you're shopping on before finalizing your purchase!

f23:
Bags expand your inventory by increasing the number of available slots. 

Every character starts with a permanent 16-slot backpack and four additional bag slots to equip larger or specialized containers.
f40:
Bags expand your inventory space by increasing the number of item slots your character can carry. Every character begins with a permanent 16-slot backpack and has four additional bag slots where larger or specialized bags can be equipped to hold even more items.

Bags come in a variety of sizes and types, and can be purchased from vendors, found on the Auction House, looted from enemies, or bought from the Ascension Store. Some bags function as containers for specific items only, like gathering or crafting materials, and cannot hold other objects.

To manage your inventory, press (Hotkey B) to open your main backpack. Pressing (Hotkey Shift + B) will open all of your equipped bags at once, making it easier to organize and access your items.

f23:
Bloodforged equipment is Soulbound PvE gear that has been transformed into Bind-on-Equip PvP gear.

To Bloodforge an item, it must first be Soulbound, then combined with a Bloody Jar which is available to purchase from Nozdormu.
f40:
Bloodforged equipment is Soulbound PvE gear that has been transformed into Bind-on-Equip PvP gear. This process allows previously Soulbound items to become tradable.

To Bloodforge an item, it must first be bound to you. Then, you can combine it with a Bloody Jar, which can be purchased from Nozdormu.

Bloodforged gear can also drop from enemies (at maximum level) or be looted from defeated players slain in High-Risk PvP Mode.

f23:
The Guild Bank is a large shared storage accessible at major cities where guild members can store and share items or gold. 

Guild leaders control permissions and can purchase additional tabs for gold as the Guild grows.
f40:
The Guild Bank is a large shared storage space available to members of a Guild. It allows players to store and share items, materials, and gold within their community, making it easier to manage resources collectively.

You can access the Guild Bank at special NPCs located in major cities. Guild leaders have control over permissions, deciding which members can deposit or withdraw items and funds to maintain organization and security.

As the Guild grows, additional storage tabs can be purchased to expand the Guild Bank. This extra space helps support group activities like raiding, crafting, and other events, by providing plenty of room for important items.

f23: The Personal Bank is a summonable container that provides expanded storage for your character. It can only be summoned in rested areas or raid instances.
f40:
The Personal Bank is a summonable container that provides extra storage exclusively for your current character. It allows convenient access to additional bags without needing to visit a physical Bank. 

Unlike the Realm-Wide Bank, the Personal Bank is character-specific and can only be accessed by the character who owns it. It can be summoned only in rested areas, such as in an Inn or a Capital City, or in Raid instances.

This item is part of the Vanity Collection and can be obtained from the Auction House or purchased on the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

f23:
The Realm-Wide Bank is a summonable storage accessible by all of your characters on the same realm, making it easy to transfer items between them. 

It cannot store Soulbound items and can only be summoned in rested areas or Raid instances.
f40:
The Realm-Wide Bank is a summonable storage system accessible by all your characters on the same server, enabling easy item transfer between alts without relying on the mailbox. It holds a wide variety of non-Soulbound items but cannot store or transfer Soulbound gear.

Unlike the Personal Bank, the Realm-Wide Bank is realm-specific and can be accessed by any character on that particular server. It can be summoned only in rested areas, such as in an Inn or a Capital City, or in Raid instances. 

This item is part of the Vanity Collection and can be obtained from the Auction House or purchased on the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

f23:
The Bank lets you store a large number of items and can be expanded by adding Bag slots to increase your storage space. 

This storage is unique to each character and can be accessed in any major city.
f40:
The Bank is personal storage that allows you to safely retain extra items, materials, and gear that without cluttering your inventory. Each character has their own unique Bank, meaning items stored here are not shared across your account or other characters.

By default, your Bank offers a limited number of storage slots, but you can expand its capacity by placing Bags into the additional Bank Bag slots. If you still need more room, consider purchasing a Personal Bank or a Realm-Wide Bank from the Auction House for in-game currency, or from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

You can access your bank in any Capital City. Use the Map Lens and search for bankers to highlight their location on your mini-map or ask a guard for directions!

Alternatively, you could summon a Treasure Keeper Companion who allows remote access to your bank without the need to return to a city.

f23:
A character’s base health is the starting amount of health points before any talents, buffs, or equipment are applied. 

This represents your character’s unmodified health pool, which many abilities and mechanics use as a reference for mana costs or scaling effects.
f40:
Base Health is the foundational amount of health points (HP) your character has before any modifiers from equipment, Talents, buffs, or enchants are applied. It represents your character’s unmodified durability, determined by your class and level.

This value is important because many abilities, scaling effects, and mechanics (especially those related to healing, tanking, or health-based damage) calculate their effects as a percentage of base health, not your total HP after bonuses.

For example, if a talent or spell states that it heals for “5% of Base Health,” it will always refer to that unmodified amount, ensuring consistent scaling regardless of your gear or buffs.

f23:
A character’s base mana is the starting amount of mana points before any Talents, buffs, or equipment are applied. 

This represents your character’s unmodified mana pool, which many abilities and mechanics use as a reference for mana costs or scaling.
f40:
Base Mana is the default amount of mana a character has before any bonuses from gear, Talents, buffs, or enchantments are applied. It represents your character’s unmodified mana pool, which many abilities and mechanics use as a reference for mana costs or scaling.

This value is important because many abilities, scaling effects, and mechanics (especially those related to spellcasting) calculate their effects as a percentage of base mana, not your total mana pool after bonuses.

For example, if a Talent or spell states that it costs “5% of Base Mana,” it will always refer to that unmodified amount, ensuring consistent scaling regardless of your gear or buffs.

f23:
Donation Points (DP) are a premium currency used in the Ascension Store to purchase cosmetics, Heirlooms, Bags, Companions, and a wide range of convenience items. 

DP allows players to support the development of the server while unlocking useful features and stylish gear.
f40:
Donation Points (DP) are a premium currency used in the Ascension Store to purchase cosmetics, Heirlooms, Bags, Companions, and a wide range of convenience items. DP allows players to support the development of the server while unlocking useful features and stylish gear.

When you purchase Donation Points, you receive equal amounts of both DP and RDP (Realm Donation Points). While your DP balance is shared across your entire account, different realms may use different currencies. Live realms use DP, while PTR or testing realms (such as Conquest of Azeroth during its testing phase) use RDP.

RDP functions like DP but is exclusive to PTR realms. When a PTR realm graduates to a live realm, it resets its economy, and all future purchases must be made with standard DP.

Most items purchased with these points are tradable and can be found on the Auction House or exchanged with Tiraxis for in-game currency, giving even non-donating players a way to access premium content.

You can access the store through the Ascension launcher or at ascension.gg/store.

f23:
Bazaar Tokens can be used to buy items from Tiraxis. 

With these tokens, you can obtain cosmetics, convenience items, Heirlooms, and Stones of Retreat or use them to auto-complete the Call Board Daily Quest.
f40:
Bazaar Tokens are a premium Currency used to purchase a wide range of items from Tiraxis, a Vendor located in the Auction House of every Capital City. These tokens can be purchased from the Auction House or bought from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

Once obtained, you can exchange them for:

- Cosmetic Equipment, Mounts, Companions, spell effects, and wings
- Convenient Donation Items such as the Book of Ascension or a Craftsman’s Codex
- Heirlooms that increase levelling speed
- Stones of Retreat for quick travel around the world

In addition to shopping at Tiraxis, Bazaar Tokens can be used to auto-complete the Call Board Daily Quest, making them a valuable catch-up tool for players with limited time or those aiming to progress quickly through end-game content.

f23: Enchanting is a Primary Profession and a Crafting Profession that enhances equipment with magical effects, granting additional stats and unique bonuses. Enchanting relies on disenchanting Uncommon, Rare, or Epic Quality gear into crafting materials but destroys the item in the process.
f40: Enchanting is a Primary Profession and a Crafting Profession that enhances weapons and armor with magical effects. To begin, you need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn enchanting. Once trained, you can collect materials by disenchanting equipment of uncommon, rare, or epic quality. This process destroys the item and converts it into materials like dusts, essences, and shards, which are used to create enchantments. As you progress, you unlock Recipes, called formulas, that let you apply specific enchantments to gear. Enchanting your own gear only uses materials, but selling or storing enchantments requires Enchanting Vellum from Vendors. To avoid vellum costs, use the Trade window to enchant other players gear, including Soulbound items. To perform enchantments, you need to craft a rod. Higher-level enchantments require more advanced rods, so upgrade your skill tools as you progress. For players managing multiple professions, an Ethereal Tool Dispenser can consolidate Profession tools into a single inventory slot and is available from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP) or from the Auction House for gold.

f23:
Bedlam bullions are awarded for completing Manastorm levels for the first time, with higher levels granting more bullions. 

They’re stored in your Currency tab (Hotkey C -> Currency) and can be spent at Millhouse Manastorm to purchase cosmetics and convenience items.
f40:
Bedlam bullions are a Realm-Bound Currency earned by completing Manastorm levels for the first time. Each new level cleared rewards you with a set amount of bullions, and higher levels grant more, encouraging steady progression through the endless dungeon. However, re-clearing previously completed levels does not award additional bullions, only your first clear of each floor counts.

You can view your current amount of bedlam bullions in the Currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab). Because they’re Realm-Bound, bullions can’t be traded or sold to other players, but they’re shared across all of your characters on the same realm.

You can spend your bedlam bullions at Millhouse Manastorm for cosmetic equipment, convenience items, novelty toys, Tamed Pet appearances, and Companions.

f23:
The Beginner’s Book of Ascension is a special trainer that can teach any character all class abilities up to level 20, regardless of class. 

You’ll find this floating book in starter zones and early-level questing hubs.
f40:
The Beginner’s Book of Ascension is a NPC that functions as a universal Class Trainer. Found in starter zones and early-level questing hubs, this book allows any character, regardless of class, to learn all available class abilities up to level 20.

With the Beginner’s Book of Ascension, you won’t need to hunt down a specific Class Trainer in the early game, making it a great tool for getting started quickly. 

You can easily locate the Beginner’s Book of Ascension using the Map Lens on your mini-map. Just search for “Class Trainer”, and any nearby Books will be marked for you.

After reaching level 20, you’ll need to visit your class-specific trainer or use a Book of Ascension to continue learning new spells and higher ranks.

f23: The Beginner’s Book of Artisans is a special trainer that can teach any profession up to a skill level of 75. You’ll find this floating book in starter zones and early-level questing hubs.
f40:
The Beginner’s Book of Artisans is a NPC that acts as a universal Profession Trainer. Found in starter zones and early-level questing hubs, this book allows you to learn any Primary Profession or Secondary Skill up to a skill level of 75, making it an excellent way to get started without needing to hunt down specific trainers.

This early-game convenience helps you jump into crafting, gathering, and Profession leveling without delay, no matter which Profession you’re aiming for, be it Mining, Alchemy, Engineering, or others.

You can easily locate the Beginner’s Book of Artisans using the Map Lens on your mini-map. Just search for “Profession Trainers”, and any nearby books will be marked for you.

Once you’ve passed skill level 75, you’ll need to visit a full Profession Trainer in a larger hub, or use the Book of Artisans Companion, to continue learning Recipes and advancing your skill further.

f23:
There are four types of armor: Cloth, Leather, Mail, and Plate. The type of gear you should equip depends on your playstyle. 

Each armor type provides a different amount of Armor, with Cloth providing the least amount of protection and Plate providing the most.
f40:
Armor Type determines the kind of gear your character can equip and how much physical protection it provides. There are four types of equipment: Cloth, Leather, Mail, and Plate.

Different armors offer different levels of Armor rating, which reduces incoming physical damage.

- Cloth offers the least protection but is commonly used by casters for its magical bonuses.
- Leather provides moderate defense and is favored by agile classes.
- Mail offers more hardiness but still some dexterity and is used by archers or armored casters.
- Plate delivers the highest physical resistance and is worn by a melee fighter or a Tank.

The type of equipment you should wear is determined by your playstyle as choosing isn’t just about defense. Each piece of gear often comes with stats tailored for specific roles, like Intellect for casters or Strength for melee builds. Wearing the proper equipment for your role ensures both survivability and performance in combat.

f23:
Blacksmithing is a Primary Profession and a Crafting Profession that can create melee weapons, mail and plate equipment, item enhancements, and so much more.

Blacksmithing is reliant on Mining for materials.
f40:
Blacksmithing is a Primary Profession and a Crafting Profession for players who want to forge powerful weapons, armor, and tools using metal and other materials. Blacksmiths create a wide range of equipment used mostly by melee-focused builds, as well as components essential for other Professions like Enchanting and Engineering. 

To begin, you’ll need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn Blacksmithing. Once trained, you can start collecting or purchasing the required materials, primarily ores and bars gathered and smelted by Mining.

As you level up, you'll unlock Recipes called Plans that teach you how to forge specific weapons, armor pieces, enhancements, and tools.

Blacksmithing requires access to an anvil and a blacksmith hammer. Anvils are found in most towns and cities near forge areas, while the blacksmith hammer can be purchased from Vendors and must be in your inventory to craft. 

For those managing multiple professions, investing in an Ethereal Tool Dispenser can be helpful as this item consolidates all Profession tools into a single inventory slot and is available from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP) or from the Auction House for in-game gold.

f23: Block is a secondary stat that requires a shield to be equipped. It allows you to absorb a portion of incoming damage when blocking an attack from an enemy in front of you or to your sides.
f40:
Block is a secondary stat that requires an equipped shield. It allows you to absorb a portion of incoming damage when you block an attack from an enemy in front of you or to your sides.

A higher block rating increases both your chance to block attacks and the amount of damage reduced when you do block, helping improve your survivability in combat.

You can view your block rating in Character Info (Hotkey C).

f23:
Bonzo bolts are awarded for completing Manastorm levels, with higher levels granting more bolts. 

They’re stored in your Currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab) and can be spent at Cogsworth to purchase and upgrade Manastorm Spells.
f40:
Bonzo bolts are a unique Currency earned by progressing through the Manastorm. Each time you complete a level, you receive bonzo bolts, with higher levels awarding more bolts. Re-clearing previously completed levels will always grant a small amount of bolts making them worth repeating.

Bonzo bolts are stored in your Currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab) and are Realm-Bound, meaning they can be used by any character on your server.

These bolts are primarily used to interact with Cogsworth, a vendor located next to Millhouse Manastorm near the entrance of Stormwind or Orgrimmar. With bonzo bolts, you can purchase new Manastorm Spells or upgrade existing ones to more powerful versions.

f23:
The Book of Ascension is a Class Trainer in the form of a summonable companion that teaches your character all of their class abilities. 

You can use another player’s book to train or summon your own to automatically learn abilities as you level.
f40:
The Book of Ascension is a powerful, summonable companion pet that acts as an all-in-one Class Trainer. When summoned, it allows your character to learn all available class abilities, including new spells as you level and higher ranks of existing spells no matter where you are in the world.

This makes it an incredibly useful quality-of-life tool, especially for players on the go or those playing in zones far from major cities. You can even use another player’s Book of Ascension if they’ve summoned theirs nearby, making it an asset in group settings as well. However, if you have the book as on of your own Companions, it will automatically train your new spells and ranks as you level up!

You can buy a Book of Ascension from the Auction House or Tiraxis for in-game Currency. Alternatively, you can purchase one from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

The Book of Ascension is a companion saved in your Vanity Collection, so it’s available to all your characters on the same realm once unlocked.

f23: The Book of Artisans is a Profession Trainer in the form of a summonable Companion that can teach your character any Profession or Recipe that’s available from other Profession Trainers.
f40:
The Book of Artisans is a convenient, summonable companion pet that functions as a portable Profession Trainer. When summoned, it allows your character to learn any Profession or trainer-taught Recipe, just as if you were speaking to a trainer in a capital city or quest hub.

This tool is especially valuable for players leveling professions across multiple characters or frequently changing Profession setups. With the Book of Artisans, there’s no need to travel across the world to visit individual trainers.

You can buy a Book of Artisans from the Auction House or Tiraxis for in-game Currency. Alternatively, you can purchase one from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

The Book of Artisans is one of the companions saved in your Vanity Collection, making it available to all your characters on the same realm once unlocked.

f23: Archetypes are pre-built classless builds designed to help newcomers get started by automatically granting spells, talents, and enchantments as you play. Chosen in character creation, they offer structured introductions to Ascension’s mechanics, and can be disabled anytime by visiting Stony Tark.
f40:
Archetypes are pre-constructed builds engineered to give newcomers a structured introduction to Ascension's classless system.

When you are creating your character, click archetype and you’ll be prompted to choose a role and playstyle. Once you do, you’ll see epic classless builds pulled from the Hero Architect based on your choices. 

Pick one, and you’ll enter the world as that archetype with everything you need to start playing. 

As you play, you’ll automatically learn your archetype’s spells, talents, and mystic enchantments, so you can take on greater challenges recommended if you're new to Ascension or to Azeroth as a whole, these character builds will help introduce you to Ascension game mechanics and the world of Azeroth while you imagine your ultimate hero.  

If you ever want to opt-out of your archetype while you are playing, visit Stony Tark and turn off the Build-Draft Game Mode.

f23: Character Advancement (Hotkey N) lets you manage your Wildcard build, reroll spells and Talents, use Skill Cards, save Specializations, and switch between custom loadouts.
f40: The Character Advancement panel (Hotkey N) is your central interface for customizing and managing your character build on Ascension classless realms. In Wildcard Mode, this menu lets you review your current spells and Talents, reroll unwanted rolls with Scrolls of Fortune, browse possible abilities, and plan stronger combinations. It also includes Skill Cards, where you can view your account-wide collection and activate cards during the early levels of a build. You can save and manage Specializations to switch between different builds, and each Specialization has its own build setup so you can experiment without overwriting your other specs.

f23: The Call Board offers a wide variety of daily quests covering all types of content. These quests provide valuable end-game rewards and catch-up Currency. If you fall behind you can auto-complete your quests using gold or Bazaar Tokens.
f40: Call Board Daily Quests offer a wide selection of objectives spanning PvE, PvP, world content, professions, and more. Available through the Call Board in each Capital City, these quests are a key source of end-game rewards and daily progression. Completing Call Board dailies can earn Marks of Ascension, Honor Points, Call Board Caches, and other catch-up rewards. The Call Board stores up to 7 days worth of quests, refreshing with new objectives every day. This system gives you flexibility to log in on your own schedule without missing out. If you fall behind or are short on time, you can auto-complete missed dailies using gold or Bazaar Tokens.

If you fall behind you can auto-complete your quests using gold or Bazaar Tokens.
f40:
Call Board Daily Quests offer a wide selection of objectives spanning all types of content including PvE, PvP, world content, professions, and more. Available through the Call Board in each Capital City, these quests are a key source of end-game rewards, making them a vital part of daily progression.

Completing Call Board Dailies can earn you Marks of Ascension, Honor Points, and Call Board Caches.

The Call Board stores up to 7 days’ worth of quests, refreshing with new objectives every day. This system gives you the flexibility to log in on your own schedule without missing out. If you fall behind or are short on time, you can auto-complete missed dailies using gold or Bazaar Tokens.

f23: Character Advancement (Hotkey N) allows you to customize your build by selecting Talents and abilities, importing builds with the Hero Architect, saving a Specialization, and easily switching between custom loadouts.
f40:
The Character Advancement panel (Hotkey N) is your go-to interface for customizing and managing your character’s build on Ascension’s classless realms. It offers powerful tools for shaping your playstyle, whether you're creating a build from scratch or importing a community favorite.

This menu lets you choose your Primary Attribute to shape your build’s core stat focus, assign an ability or Talent Essence to your next desired spell, and browse all potential abilities and Talents - making it easy to search for synergy rolls and plan powerful combinations. 

You can also access the Hero Architect to quickly importat a community curated build without manually reassigning abilities and Talents.

Additionally, you can save and manage your Specialization to switch between builds without manually reassigning abilities or Talents, and link a Mystic Enchant Specialization as well as one of your Equipment Sets so your gear and enchants update automatically when swapping builds.

f23:
Call Board Caches are earned by completing the Call Board Daily Quest and offer a great way to catch up to current content. 

They have a high chance to contain gear upgrades, including Dungeon and Raid gear from all released content up to the most recent Raid.
f40:
These caches are reward chests earned by completing the Call Board Daily Quest. Designed as a catch-up mechanic, these caches are ideal for helping players quickly gear up for current content, especially if you're returning to the game or leveling a fresh character.

Each cache has a high chance to contain gear upgrades, from Dungeon gear to epic Raid loot from all previously released content, scaling up to the most recently released Raid. If you receive a cache from a daily quest requiring PvP activities, the gear from your cache will be Bloodforged.

These chests offer a reliable alternative to repetitive farming, giving you access to relevant power gains even if you're behind the current progression curve. They're especially helpful for preparing alts or off-specs for group content.

f23: The Character Advancement panel (Hotkey N) is your central hub for customizing talent trees, managing multiple specializations, and tracking class-specific spells, giving you full control over your build and the flexibility to adapt your playstyle.
f40:
The Character Advancement panel (Hotkey N) is the central hub for customizing your character. This menu allows you to allocate points across your class’ three distinct talent trees, helping you shape your playstyle as you level and progress into endgame content.

From this menu, you can spend talent points to unlock powerful passive effects and abilities that support your chosen specialization. 

It also allows you to save and manage multiple talent specializations, making it easy to switch between different builds at any time. You can link your Mystic Enchanting Specialization and Equipment Sets to your build so that your gear and enchants update automatically when you swap. 

Additionally, the menu displays all your class-specific spells in one organized place, helping you track what you’ve learned and plan future upgrades.

f23:
While leveling, the Call Board guides you to the next questing zone to continue your journey. At max level, it offers daily and weekly quests with valuable rewards. 

You can find the Call Board near the entrance of your Capital City.
f40:
The Call Board is a useful quest hub found near the entrances of every Capital City, designed to help players stay on track throughout their journey.

While leveling, the Call Board directs you to the next appropriate questing area, ensuring smooth zone progression and helping you avoid out-leveling content. It’s especially handy for new players or those unsure of where to go next.

At the maximum level, the Call Board offers daily and weekly quests that provide a variety of rewards, including Marks of Ascension, valuable Currency, rare or epic equipment, and more. These quests often encourage players to revisit dungeons, complete world events, or engage in other content that contributes to their overall progression.

For added convenience, you can acquire a portable call board, which lets you access these quests from anywhere in the world. You can buy a call board for your faction or a neutral one that can be used by all characters from the Auction House or from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

f23:
Capital cities are central social hubs offering key services like the Bank, Call Board, and Auction House.

Stormwind (SW) is the capital of the Alliance, while Orgrimmar (Org) is for the Horde.
f40:
Capital cities are the main social and logistical hubs for players of each faction. These cities serve as vital gathering points where players can access essential services such as the Bank for storing and retrieving items, the Auction House to buy and sell goods with other players, and the Call Board for picking up quests and coordinating group activities.

For the Alliance, Stormwind stands as the grand capital city, an enormous medieval-style kingdom filled with vendors, trainers, guild halls, and iconic landmarks. Meanwhile, the Horde’s capital is Orgrimmar, a fortified city built into the harsh landscapes of Durotar, reflecting the faction’s rugged and tribal culture.

Once players reach level 20, they receive a valuable convenience item called the Scroll of Retreat. This item is automatically added to their Vanity Collection and allows them to instantly teleport back to their faction’s capital city, making travel and access to services much easier, especially after completing quests or dungeons far from home.

Capital cities also act as social hubs where players can meet, trade, form groups, and participate in various in-game events.

f23: The Character Advancement panel (Hotkey N) is your central hub for customizing your class and talent tree, managing multiple specializations, and importing community curated loadouts, giving you full control over your build and the flexibility to adapt your playstyle.
f40:
The Character Advancement panel (Hotkey N) is where you define and develop your build. Every class in CoA features multiple specializations, each with its own talent tree and unique class tree, offering a deep and customizable path for character progression.

From this menu, you can select or switch your Specialization, choosing between distinct playstyles within your class. 

You’ll spend points in your class tree to unlock signature abilities and defining mechanics, and invest in your talent tree to boost core stats, survivability, or damage potential. 

The menu also lets you import builds from the community or create your own to share. You can save multiple specializations and freely swap between them, making it easy to shift roles or strategies as needed.

f23:
Character Info (Hotkey C) displays your equipped gear and current stats. Hover over any stat or item for detailed information. 

From this menu, you can save equipment sets and assign a cosmetic title to your character.
f40:
The Character Info panel (Hotkey C) is your central hub for managing your character’s gear, stats, and key progression details.

It shows all currently equipped items and provides a full breakdown of combat stats like Strength, Intellect, Spell Power, Critical Strike chance, and more. Hovering over any stat or item reveals a tooltip with detailed explanations and comparisons.

From this menu, you can also access the equipment manager to save and assign equipment sets or choose a cosmetic title from those you've unlocked.

f23: Character Info (Hotkey C) displays your equipped gear and current stats. Hover over any stat or item for detailed information. From this menu, you can save equipment sets, assign a cosmetic title to your character, and review character currencies.

It shows all currently equipped items and provides a full breakdown of combat stats like Strength, Intellect, Spell Power, Critical Strike chance, and more. Hovering over any stat or item reveals a tooltip with detailed explanations. f23:
Class trainers specialize in one class and can teach you new spells as well as higher ranks of existing spells. 

To find a class trainer, use the Map Lens to locate one on your mini-map or ask a guard in a Capital City.
f40:
Class trainers are NPCs that specialize in a single class and allow you to learn new abilities and higher ranks of spells you’ve acquired. 

You will only be able to train at your corresponding class trainer. These trainers teach you all the abilities and upgrades available to your chosen class as you level.

You can locate class trainers by speaking to a guard in any Capital City or by using the Map Lens on your mini-map to highlight nearby trainers. They're typically found in class-specific training halls or districts.

For added convenience, players can use the Book of Ascension regardless if it's their own companion or another player’s. This all-in-one tool functions as a universal class trainer, allowing you to learn any available spells or ranks without needing to travel.

f23:
Cogsworth sells Manastorm Spells and upgrades in exchange for Bonzo Bolts. 

Cogsworth can be found next to Millhouse Manastorm near the entrance of Stormwind or Orgrimmar.
f40:
Cogsworth is an NPC vendor located near Millhouse Manastorm at the entrance of your Capital City. He plays an important role in the Manastorm system, offering a variety of Manastorm Spells and upgrade items in exchange for Bonzo Bolts which is a Currency earned by progressing through the Manastorm.

The items Cogsworth sells are designed to enhance your effectiveness in the Manastorm, from powerful spells that help in tougher encounters to useful upgrades that provide more control, survivability, or utility as you climb.

f40:
Class trainers are NPCs that specialize in a single class and allow you to learn new abilities and higher ranks of spells you’ve acquired. 

In Ascension’s classless system, you’ll often need to visit multiple class trainers to fully upgrade your character’s unique combination of skills, for example, visiting both a mage and a warrior trainer if you’ve picked spells from both classes.

You can locate class trainers by speaking to a guard in any Capital City or by using the Map Lens on your mini-map to highlight nearby trainers. They're typically found in class-specific training halls or districts.

For added convenience, players can use the Book of Ascension regardless if it's their own companion or another player’s. This all-in-one tool functions as a universal class trainer, allowing you to learn any available spells or ranks without needing to travel.

f23:
Conquest of Azeroth (CoA) is an Ascension realm featuring 21 unique classes, each with at least three Specializations offering a total of 69 fresh ways to play. 

Enjoy new spells, visuals, custom content, and systems, all crafted to provide a unique Vanilla+ experience.
f40:
Conquest of Azeroth (CoA) is a specialized Ascension realm designed to deliver a fresh and exciting Vanilla+ experience. It features 21 unique classes, each offering at least three distinct Specializations, for a total of 69 innovative ways to play.

On Conquest of Azeroth, players enjoy brand-new spells, unique visuals, custom content, and specialized game systems crafted to deepen gameplay variety and encourage experimentation. This realm is perfect for those seeking to journey through Azeroth with a twist, combining nostalgia with creative new options that expand how you build and customize your character.

To join the current CoA playtesting server, you must purchase a Conquest of Azeroth Travel Guide. This item can be obtained through the Auction House or directly from the Ascension Store for Donation Points. Using the guide unlocks access to this unique realm, allowing you to explore its many custom features.

f23:
Cooking is a Secondary Skill and a Crafting Profession that uses raw meat and fish to create consumables that restore health and mana and provide beneficial buffs.

Cooking relies on materials looted from beasts or gathered through Fishing.
f40:
Cooking is a Secondary Skill and a Crafting Profession, focused on preparing food that grants temporary buffs, restores health, and improves combat effectiveness. Cooks create a wide variety of consumables that can boost Primary Attributes and secondary stats.

To begin, you’ll need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn cooking. Once trained, you can start collecting the ingredients required for your Recipes. Cooking materials are primarily gathered from beasts in the open world, caught through Fishing, or purchased from Vendors.

As you level up, you’ll unlock Recipes that teach you how to prepare specific meals and feasts to share with your friends. Higher-level meals often grant stronger and more specialized buffs, making them highly sought after for Raid preparation or competitive gameplay.

Cooking does not require any special tool to craft, however, players often pair cooking with Fishing to maintain a steady supply of materials.

f23:
Companions are smaller, non-combat pets that can be summoned alongside a Tamed Pet. 

Some companions offer services such as the Book of Ascension, the Treasure Keeper, or the Lootbot 3000.
f40:
Companions are small, non-combat pets that accompany your character alongside your Tamed Pet. While they don’t participate in battles, many companions provide useful services that enhance your gameplay experience.

Treasure Keeper - Serves as a portable Bank.
Book of Ascension - Serves as a portable Class Trainer.
Book of Artisans - Serves as a portable Profession Trainer.
Lootbot 3000 - Automatically loots all the defeated enemies around you so you don’t have to. (You can combine this with the Loot-Transfigurator 5000 for your lootbot to take the appearance of any of your other learned companions.)

You can view and summon your companions through the Pets Tab (Hotkey Shift + P -> Companion Tab).

f23:
Courier Malik, found in city Auction Houses, allows players to send unbound vanity items (those stored in the Vanity Collection) between the Seasonal Server and Area: 52. 

Items sent this way become instantly bound to your Vanity Collection and cannot be traded.
f40:
Courier Malik is an NPC located inside the Auction Houses of your Capital City. He facilitates the transfer of unbound vanity items (such as mounts, pets, toys, and other cosmetics) between the Seasonal Realm and Area: 52 servers.

Only non-consumable vanity items that can be saved in your Vanity Collection are eligible for transfer through Courier Malik. Consumable items cannot be sent this way. When items are transferred, they become instantly bound to your Vanity Collection on the receiving server and cannot be traded, mailed, or sold, ensuring your cosmetic collection remains personal and secure.

The transfer process is simple and free, making it an essential tool for maintaining and unifying your Vanity Collection across different realms.

f23:
A Craftsman’s Codex is a consumable item that unlocks an additional Primary Profession slot for that character. 

Codexes can be bought for various in-game currencies as well as from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).
f40:
A Craftsman’s Codex is a consumable item that unlocks an additional Primary Profession slot for the character it is used on. This allows you to learn and level a third Primary Profession, expanding your crafting and gathering capabilities beyond the usual two-slot limit.

You can use multiple codexes on a single character (one for each additional profession slot) until you have unlocked every Primary Profession. This gives you the freedom to master every crafting and gathering trade if you wish.

You can purchase a codex off of the Auction House, from Tiraxis or from Nozdormu for in-game Currency, or from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

f23:
Critical Strike damage bonus is a stat that boosts the percentage damage dealt when you land a Critical Strike, making your critical hits even more powerful. 

This bonus can be increased through various Talents and abilities.
f40:
Critical Strike damage bonus is a stat that boosts the percentage damage dealt when you land a Critical Strike, making your critical hits even more powerful. This bonus can be increased through various Talents and abilities.

By default, physical critical strikes deal 200% damage, while spell critical strikes deal 175% damage. 

However, these base values can be enhanced by increasing your damage bonus.

f23: Crafting Professions use materials gathered from the world, or looted from enemies, to create equipment, enhancements, and consumables.
f40:
Crafting professions are a category of Primary Profession that allow players to use materials gathered from the world or looted from enemies to create equipment, enhancements, and consumables.

The available crafting professions are:

Alchemy - Brew potions, elixirs, and flasks that provide powerful temporary buffs.
Blacksmithing - Forge weapons, armor, and useful metal items.
Enchanting - Enchance your gear with magic, improving stats and adding unique effects.
Engineering - Create gadgets, explosives, and special items often useful in utility situations.
Leatherworking - Craft leather and mail armor, as well as armor kits and other useful items.
Tailoring - Sew cloth armor, powerful spellthreads, and Bags.
Jewelcrafting - Cut gems used to socket gear and craft jewelry. (Available in Burning Crusade.)

Crafting Professions are a great way to earn gold, supply yourself or your Guild with amazing enhancements and equipment, and can give you an edge in challenging content.

f23: Critical Strike Damage Bonus is a stat that boosts the percentage damage dealt when you land a Critical Strike, making your critical hits even more powerful. This bonus can be increased through various Talents and abilities.
f40: Critical Strike Damage Bonus is a stat that boosts the percentage damage dealt when you land a Critical Strike, making your critical hits even more powerful. This bonus can be increased through various Talents and abilities. By default, physical critical strikes deal 200% damage, while spell critical strikes deal 175% damage. Additional Critical Strike Damage Bonus increases the damage multiplier further, making it especially valuable for builds that rely on frequent critical hits.

f23: Critical Strike is a secondary stat that increases your chance for attacks and healing spells to be extra effective.
f40:
Critical Strike is a secondary stat that increases your chance for attacks and healing spells to be extra effective. Critical hits deal significantly more damage or healing, making them a powerful way to boost your overall power in combat.

By default, physical critical strikes deal 200% damage, while spell criticals heal or deal 175% of their normal value. These numbers can be further improved by increasing your Critical Strike Damage Bonus.

You can find your current critical strike rating in Character Info (Hotkey C).

f23:
Currency refers to various special tokens and points used to purchase items, services, and unique rewards. 

These points are stored in the currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab) and cannot be traded or bought on the Auction House.
f40:
Currency refers to various special tokens and points used to purchase items, services, and unique rewards. These points are not stored in your inventory and cannot be traded or bought on the Auction House. 

You can view all your currencies in the currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab).

Examples of currency are:

Honor Points
Arena Points
Marks of Ascension
Seasonal Points
Tokens of Prestige

f23:
DPS (Damage Per Second) functions both as a player’s role, and as a unit of measurement reported by addons to determine the damage output of a player or group. 

A DPS player specializes in dealing damage to enemies, aiming to reduce their health as quickly and efficiently as possible.
f40:
DPS (Damage Per Second) functions both as a player’s role, and as a unit of measurement reported by addons to determine the damage output of a player or group.

A DPS player specializes in dealing damage to enemies, aiming to reduce their health as quickly and efficiently as possible.

DPS players focus on using a variety of offensive abilities, spells, and weapon attacks to maximize their damage output while managing resources like mana, energy, or rage. They often rely on positioning, timing, and crowd control to enhance their effectiveness.

f23:
Draft Mode lets you choose one ability from three random, classless options every other level, adding variety to your build while keeping Talents customizable. 

At max level, you can use Hands of Fate (purchased with Marks of Ascension) to redraw and optimize your abilities.
f40:
Draft Mode adds a unique twist to character progression by letting you choose one ability from three random, classless options every other level. This system introduces an element of luck and creativity, encouraging you to experiment with different playstyles and combinations.

While your abilities are chosen through Draft Mode, your Talents remain fully customizable, allowing you to personalize your character’s power and strategy.

Once you reach max level, you can refine your chosen abilities using Hands of Fate, a special item purchased with Marks of Ascension. Hands of Fate let you redraw your abilities, giving you the freedom to fine-tune your build and craft the perfect setup for your playstyle.

f23:
The Dungeon Finder (Hotkey i) quickly matches you with other players for Dungeon runs based on your chosen role and Dungeon preference, teleporting you directly inside to earn Experience, gear, and rewards. 

Bonuses are often granted for random dungeons or in-demand roles, making it a fast and popular way to level and prepare for endgame content.
f40:
The Dungeon Finder is a convenient tool that quickly connects you with other players to run dungeons together. To use it, open the Dungeons and Raids menu (Hotkey i), select your preferred role (Tank, Healer, or DPS) and choose whether to queue for a specific dungeon or a random dungeon (often called Random Dungeon Finder or RDF).

Once the system finds a group, you’ll be instantly teleported to the Dungeon, where you can earn Experience, gear, and complete quests. After finishing your run, simply right-click the Dungeon finder icon on your minimap and select “Leave Dungeon” to return to the open world.

Choosing to run random dungeons or filling a role that’s in high demand often grants bonus loot and rewards, making the Dungeon Finder one of the fastest and most popular ways to level up and prepare for endgame content.

f23:
Dungeons are five-player instanced challenges featuring elite mobs, tough bosses, and valuable loot. 

You can either find their entrances in the open world or use the Dungeon Finder to join a group instantly.
f40:
Dungeons are five-player instanced challenges with elite enemies, tough bosses, and valuable loot, essential for leveling and endgame progression as they scale with your strength. 

You can access them through entrances across the open world or with the Dungeon Finder (RDF), which matches you with a group and teleports you inside. More difficult dungeons aren’t available through RDF due to difficulty, requiring you to manually form a Party (often via World Chat) and travel to the entrance. There are four types of dungeons:

Normal Dungeon – Available while leveling or shortly after reaching max level. A good place to learn boss mechanics and earn baseline gear.

Heroic Dungeon – Tougher versions designed for max-level characters. Enemies hit harder, and bosses drop better loot, including Marks of Triumph or Badges of Justice.

Mythic Dungeon – Even more challenging, with stronger mobs and enhanced mechanics. Mythic dungeons are typically run with organized groups aiming for high performance and better loot.

Mythic+ – A competitive, timed version of Mythic dungeons that scales in difficulty with each level. Completing these challenges rewards powerful gear and seasonal rewards.

f23: Equipment durability decreases during combat and death, and when it reaches zero, your gear becomes broken and unusable and must be fixed at a repair NPC who can be located using the Map Lens.
f40:
Durability is a system that tracks how much wear and tear your equipment takes during gameplay.  Weapons and armor have a durability value that gradually decreases as you engage in combat. Taking damage, using abilities, and especially dying all contribute to durability loss.

When a piece of gear reaches zero durability, it breaks. Broken items lose all of their stat bonuses, armor value, and effects, making them completely unusable until repaired.

To restore durability, visit any repair Vendor, typically found in towns, quest hubs, and capital cities. These NPCs can be quickly located using the Map Lens by searching for 'Repair.' Repairing gear costs gold, with more powerful items generally requiring more to fix.

Keeping your gear in good condition is vital, especially before entering dungeons, battlegrounds, or high-risk zones. Don’t wait until something breaks mid-fight, repair early and often.

f23:
Donation items are items obtained from the Ascension Store. These items can be bought from the online shop for Donation Points or found from the Auction House for in-game currency. 

Most donation items are either consumables, or can be found saved within your Vanity Collection.
f40:
Donation items are special items obtained through the Ascension Store, typically purchased using Donation Points (DP). These items are designed to provide convenience, cosmetic customization, and utility, without offering unfair power advantages in competitive content.

While most donation items are acquired through the online store, many can also be found on the Auction House, allowing players to purchase them with in-game currency instead of Donation Points. This makes them accessible to all players, whether or not they spend real money.

Most donation items fall into one of two categories:

Consumables – Useful tools like a Craftsman’s Codex, an Experience booster, or Tomes of Specialization.

Vanity Collection Items – Mounts, toys, cosmetic equipment, Companions, Heirlooms, and other Realm-Bound unlocks are stored safely in your Vanity Collection, where they can be accessed by any character on the same server.

f23:
Your Mystic Enchant Collection (N -> Mystic Enchant -> Enchant Collection) stores enchants saved with Mystic Extracts. 

This menu is shared across all characters on the same realm, and is accessible at any Enchanting Altar to apply enchants to your active slots.
f40:
The Mystic Enchant Collection (Hotkey N -> Mystic Enchant Tab -> Enchant Collection Tab) is your personal library of saved mystic enchants, allowing you to easily manage, reuse, and apply enchants across all your characters on the same realm.

Within the collection menu, you can preview enchants by type and quality (even those you haven't unlocked yet) making it easy to search for the perfect addition to your build.

To add an enchant to your collection, you’ll need to use a Mystic Extract, which permanently saves a copy of that enchant for future use. Once stored, that enchant becomes available to any character you play on the realm, perfect for sharing powerful enchants across multiple builds and alternative characters.

While you can view and manage your collection anywhere, applying enchants to your Active Enchant Slots from your collection still requires a visit to an Enchanting Altar and requires Mystic Orbs.

f23:

This menu is shared across all characters on the same realm, and is accessible at any Enchanting Altar to apply enchants to your active slots.
