f23:
A Mystic Enchant Specialization is a saved loadout of your current Active Enchant Slots. 

You can change your Specialization at any time, anywhere, for no fee, without overwriting your existing setup.
f40:
A Mystic Enchant Specialization is a saved loadout of your current Active Enchant Slots, allowing you to quickly switch between different enchant setups without overwriting your existing loadout. By default, each character starts with one specialization slot.

If you want more flexibility, you can purchase additional enchant Specialization slots using a Mystic Enchanting: Specialization scroll. These scrolls are available from the Auction House or Tiraxis for in-game currency or can be bought through the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

To manage your enchant specializations use the Mystic Enchant menu (Hotkey N -> Mystic Enchant Tab).

f23:
Upon entering the Manastorm, each player receives an Endless Manastorm Potion, a reusable, short-cooldown item that restores health, energy, mana, and rage. 

Its effectiveness scales with group size, offering the most healing when solo.
f40:
Upon entering the Manastorm, every player is granted an Endless Manastorm Potion, a reusable consumable with a short cooldown that restores your health, energy, mana, and rage. This versatile potion is placed directly into your inventory and is designed to help you sustain yourself during the relentless encounters inside the Manastorm.

The potion’s effectiveness scales with group size, providing the most healing when you’re running solo, and slightly less when in larger parties. This scaling ensures it remains balanced and useful whether you’re tackling the Manastorm alone or with a full raid group.

Because the Manastorm can be punishing, keeping this potion handy on your action bar is essential for survival, allowing you to quickly recover and push deeper into the dungeon’s challenges.

f23:
Engineering is a Primary Profession and a Crafting Profession that invents powerful gadgets, explosives, and utility items that enhance the way you play.

Engineering is reliant on Mining for materials.
f40:
Engineering is a Primary Profession and a Crafting Profession for players who want to invent powerful gadgets, explosives, and utility items that can enhance the way you play. Engineers craft unique tools, devices, and trinkets that offer both combat advantages and quirky mechanical effects.

To begin, you’ll need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn engineering. Once trained, you can start collecting or purchasing the materials needed. Engineering relies heavily on metal bars and stone gathered and smelted through Mining, though many Recipes also require components sourced by Vendors, enemy loot, or parts crafted through another Profession.

As you level up, you'll unlock Recipes, known as schematics, that teach you how to craft many items that can’t be found through other professions, like teleporters, parachutes, and combat-enhancing bombs.

Crafting engineering items requires an rclight spanner, a tool that must remain in your inventory to make most schematics. For those managing multiple professions, investing in an Ethereal Tool Dispenser can be helpful as this item consolidates all Profession tools into a single inventory slot and is available from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP) or from the Auction House for in-game gold.

f23: Players can have three epic quality enchants applied in their Active Enchant Slots at a time. These enchants offer huge power boosts, new spells, and can unlock entirely new ways to play.
f40:
Epic enchants are powerful mystic enchants that you can equip in up to three Active Enchant Slots simultaneously. These enchants provide significant boosts to your character’s stats and abilities, often unlocking new spells, passive effects, or unique mechanics that can change how your character plays.

Because of their power, an epic Mystic Enchant is highly sought after by players aiming to optimize their builds or explore new playstyles. Equipping the right combination of epic enchants can elevate your effectiveness in PvE, PvP, or solo content.

f23:
The Ethereal Bazaar is a unique shop accessible through Tiraxis inside the Auction House of any Capital City. 

It offers rare and exclusive cosmetics in exchange for Bazaar Tokens but the selection rotates on a random timer and only one copy of each item is available per cycle.
f40:
The Ethereal Bazaar is a special, ever-changing shop accessible through Tiraxis inside the Auction House of any Capital City. Unlike regular Vendors, the bazaar offers a selection of rare and exclusive cosmetic items that you won’t find anywhere else.

To purchase from the Ethereal Bazaar, you’ll need Bazaar Tokens, an item purchased from the Auction House or from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP). 

Keep in mind that the bazaar’s inventory rotates on a random timer, and only one copy of each item is available per cycle. This means you’ll often compete with other players to snag these limited items before they disappear.

f23:
You can gain experience (or XP) by completing a quest, exploring a new sub-zone, gathering or crafting with a Profession, and defeating an enemy. 

Your experience bar is located at the bottom of the screen - fill it to reach the next level.
f40:
Experience (also known as XP or EXP) is the core system that tracks your character’s progress toward the next level until the maximum level is achieved. The maximum level is 60 for Vanilla, 70 for the Burning Crusade Expansion, and 80 for Wrath of the Lich King.

You gain experience by doing a wide variety of activities in the world, including:

Completing Quests
Defeating Enemies
Exploring a New Sub-Zone
Gathering or Crafting using a Profession
Participating in Battlegrounds or World Events

Your experience bar is located along the bottom of the screen, showing your progress toward the next level. Once the bar is filled, your character levels up and grants new stat points, spell options, Talents and more.

Your experience gain can be boosted by items like Heirlooms, Rested Experience from an Inn, and Hotspots, which offer bonus experience in specific zones.

f23: Expertise is a secondary stat that reduces the chance that your attacks will be dodged or parried.
f40:
Expertise is a secondary stat that reduces the chance your attacks will be dodged or parried by enemies. This means your attacks are more likely to land successfully, improving your overall damage and combat effectiveness.

You can find your current expertise in Character Info (Hotkey C).

f23:
You can save gear loadouts using the Equipment Manager (Hotkey C -> Equipment Manager Tab). 

Switching sets will automatically equip the appropriate items from your inventory or bank, making it easy to swap builds on the fly.
f40:
Equipment Sets let you quickly swap between different gear loadouts using the equipment manager (Hotkey C -> Equipment Manager Tab) a built-in tool designed to make changing builds fast and efficient. 

The equipment manager allows you to save your current gear as a named set, making it easy to switch between setups. When you activate a saved set, the system will automatically equip the correct items whether they’re in your inventory or stored in your bank.

You can also assign specific equipment sets to your Specialization, so your gear automatically swaps to match the build you're using.

f23:
Fel Commutation is a form of insurance for High-Risk PvP, letting you protect up to three specific pieces of gear from being dropped on death. 

A small gold fee is charged each time you die while protected.
f40:
Fel Commutation is a special gear protection system used in High-Risk PvP Mode, allowing players to safeguard up to three specific pieces of equipment from being dropped when they die. It acts like a form of insurance, helping reduce the sting of PvP losses without fully removing the risk.

When you commutate, you select which three gear pieces (such as weapons, trinkets, or armor) you want to protect. If you die while flagged for high-risk, these protected items will be immune to loot drops, ensuring you keep your most valuable gear. However, a small gold fee will be automatically deducted each time fel commutation activates upon death.

You can access the Fel Commutation Portal in any Capital City by looking for its icon on the World Map or asking a guard. It’s a vital system for players diving into dangerous PvP zones, especially those carrying valuable equipment or farming high-stakes objectives.

f23:
Using a Feather of the Ancients instantly unlocks all Flightpaths for your character. 

Feathers are stored in your Vanity Collection and can be obtained from the Auction House or Tiraxis for in-game Currency, as well as the Ascension Store for Donation Points.
f40:
A Feather of the Ancients is a convenience item that instantly unlocks every Flightpath for your character within a specific expansion. It’s an invaluable tool for players who want to skip the slow process of manually discovering each Flightmaster, especially on alts or during seasonal leveling.

There are different versions of the feather for each expansion:

Kalimdor and Eastern Kingdoms – Unlocks all Vanilla (Classic) flightpaths.
Outland – Unlocks all The Burning Crusade flightpaths.
Northrend – Unlocks all Wrath of the Lich King flightpaths.

Once obtained, feathers are stored in your Vanity Collection and can be used account-wide on any character.

You can acquire Feathers of the Ancients from the Auction House or Tiraxis for in-game Currency, as well as the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

f23:
Fishing is a Secondary Skill and a Gathering Profession that allows you to gather fish and other items from bodies of water throughout the world.

The materials you catch are used in the Crafting Profession Cooking and occasionally Alchemy.
f40:
Fishing is a Secondary Skill and a Gathering Profession for players who enjoy exploring the open world while collecting natural resources. Fish gathered through this skill are used in a Crafting Profession like Alchemy or Cooking.

To get started, you’ll need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn fishing. Once trained, you can begin gathering fish, or even buried treasure, by locating the nearest body of water. Once leveling to fishing skill 100, you can use a Weather-Beaten Journal that will teach you the skill to 'Find Fish' using the Map Lens. This highlights nearby pools with schools of fish where you have a much higher chance to get specific items.

Each time you collect an item from the water, you have a chance to contribute to your Fishing skill and provide fish-based materials used directly in crafting. Different zones contain different types of fish, typically tied to level ranges and progression, so exploring new areas becomes a rewarding part of leveling the Profession.

To catch fish, you’ll need a Fishing Rod, which must be equipped and can be purchased from Vendors. You can also enhance your fishing ability by attaching lures to your rod. These can also be bought from Vendors, and will temporarily boost your fishing skill allowing you to fish in higher-level waters.

f23:
First aid is a Secondary Skill and a Crafting Profession that lets you craft bandages, which restore health over time and can be used during combat.

First aid uses cloth dropped from humanoid enemies for materials.
f40:
First Aid is a Secondary Skill and a Crafting Profession, focused on creating bandages and other medical supplies that restore health quickly in and out of combat.

To begin, you’ll need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn first aid. Once trained, you can start collecting the necessary materials, which primarily consists of cloth dropped by humanoid enemies in the open world. These materials are then processed into bandages of increasing potency as you level up this skill.

As you progress, you’ll unlock Recipes, known as manuals, that teach you how to craft stronger bandages and other healing items.

First aid does not require any tools or special crafting locations, making it one of the most accessible and low-maintenance skills to use.

f23:
Flightpaths (FP) are a fast-travel system that lets you fly between specific locations. 

To use a flightpath, you must first unlock its node by speaking to the local Flightmaster or by using a Feather of the Ancients.
f40:
Flightpaths (FP) are a fast-travel system, allowing players to quickly fly between specific, connected locations across the open world. They’re essential for cutting down travel time, especially when questing or moving between distant zones.

To use a flightpath, you must first unlock its node by speaking to the local Flightmaster. You can also instantly unlock certain nodes by using special items like the Feather of the Ancients, which reveals multiple locations at once.

However, you can only fly between nodes that are directly connected and already discovered. If you're trying to travel across multiple zones, you’ll need to have unlocked all the Flightmasters along the route, otherwise, the system won’t allow you to fly to your intended destination.

Once enough nodes are unlocked, you can chain multiple points together to create efficient travel routes, making it much easier to return to old quest hubs, dungeons, or cities.

Flightpaths are accessed through any Flightmaster, typically marked with a wing icon on your World Map and mini-map. When planning your journey, be sure to use the Map Lens to find nearby Flightmasters and keep your travel network growing.

f23:
Speaking to a flightmaster unlocks their Flightpath for future use. 

Undiscovered flightmasters are marked with a green (!) above their heads.
f40:
A flightmaster is an NPC that provides fast travel between different zones and towns across the world using a Flightpath. Speaking to a flightmaster for the first time unlocks their location, allowing you to travel back there later from other connected flightmasters.

Undiscovered flightmasters are marked with a green (!) above their heads, making them easy to spot as you explore new areas. Once unlocked, they will appear as wing icons on your World Map, showing all the places your character can fly to from any given location.

You can also use the Map Lens to highlight nearby flightmasters, helping you quickly locate the nearest point of fast travel.

f23:
Ascension’s seasonal realms are time-limited servers that reset at the end of each season. 

They often feature unique game modes and progression that begins in Vanilla content and advances through to the current patch on Area: 52.
f40:
Ascension’s seasonal realms are time-limited servers designed to offer a fresh start, unique challenges, and a competitive environment for players looking to play the game in new and exciting ways. Each season typically introduces a special game mode, such as Draft Mode, Wildcard Mode, or Felforged, encouraging players to experiment with different builds and strategies.

Progression on seasonal servers usually begins in Vanilla WoW content and gradually unlocks expansions and new systems, eventually culminating in the current patch found on Area: 52, Ascension’s permanent progression realm. This seasonal structure creates a focused, level playing field where players race for Server Firsts, dominate leaderboards, and chase exclusive cosmetic and vanity rewards.

At the end of the season, the realm is closed and characters are transferred to Area: 52, bringing their gear, titles, and seasonal rewards with them. This ensures your progress is preserved, while keeping the core seasonal journey competitive and time-bound.

f23:
Gathering professions involve exploring the world to collect resources from nodes or defeated enemies. 

These materials are essential to level a Crafting Profession.
f40:
Gathering professions are a category of Primary Profession that allows players to gather raw materials from the world to supply various a Crafting Profession.

The available gathering professions are:

Herbalism - Gather herbs used in Alchemy and other crafting recipes.
Mining - Extract ore and stone from mineral nodes, used in Blacksmithing and Engineering.
Skinning - Collect leather, hides, and scales from slain beasts, used in Leatherworking.
Woodcutting - Chop down trees to turn into lumber and turn in for quests.

Gathering professions are a great way to earn gold, supply yourself or your Guild with necessary crafting materials, and engage more deeply with the world’s diverse zones.

f23:
Guilds are player-created communities that provide social connection, facilitate group content opportunities, and exclusive perks. 

Joining a guild lets you interact with other players and share a Guild Bank with your teammates.
f40:
Guilds are player-created communities that bring adventurers together under a shared banner. Whether you’re looking for friends to chat with, teammates for Dungeons and Raids, or just a sense of belonging in the world, joining a guild opens the door to more social and rewarding gameplay.

Being part of a guild gives you access to several valuable features, including a guild chat channel as well as a Guild Bank to collect and share items with your guildmates.

To find a guild, keep an eye on the global chat for recruitment messages or check your realm’s Discord server, where many guilds advertise their goals and playstyles.

If you’d rather lead than join, you can start your own guild by visiting your faction’s Guild Master NPC, found in major cities. For a small fee, you can purchase a Guild Charter, gather a few signatures from fellow players, and form your own community from scratch.

f23: Haste (also known as speed) is a secondary stat that boosts your attack speed, casting speed, and energy regeneration, letting you unleash abilities more rapidly.
f40:
Haste (also known as speed) is a secondary stat that increases your attack speed, casting speed, and energy regeneration. This allows you to use your abilities more rapidly, improving your overall damage output and responsiveness in combat.

You can find your current haste rating in the Character Info (Hotkey C).

f23:
Hardcore Trials are challenging game modes that reward players for reaching the maximum level without dying. 

If you die during the trial, you fail the challenge, but your character can still revive and continue playing as normal.
f40:
Hardcore Trials are special challenge modes that reward players for reaching the maximum level without dying. Designed to test your skill, focus, and knowledge of the game, these Trials offer unique rewards and bragging rights to those who survive the journey from level 1 to maximum without falling in battle.

To begin a hardcore trial, your character must be level 1. Visit Stony Tark, found in your starting zone or Capital City, to activate the trial. It's important to note that you must start the trial before gaining any Experience. Additionally, you won’t be able to trade, use the mailbox, or access the Auction House until after you’ve started the challenge.

During the trial, if your character dies even once, the challenge is failed. However, unlike perma-death modes, your character will revive normally and can continue to play the game as usual, they simply won’t receive the tardcore trial rewards.

Successfully completing a hardcore trial often grants you cosmetics, titles, vanity items, or other exclusive rewards, making it a popular option for players seeking thrilling and rewarding gameplay.

f23: Haste (also known as speed) is a secondary stat that boosts your attack and casting speed, letting you unleash abilities more rapidly.
f40:
Haste (also known as speed) is a secondary stat that increases your physical attack and spell casting speed. This allows you to use your abilities more rapidly, improving your overall damage output and responsiveness in combat.

You can find your current haste rating in the Character Info (Hotkey C).

f23:
A Healer specializes in mending damage and keeping their group alive during combat. 

Using healing spells, buffs, and protective abilities, healers ensure their teammates survival and are essential in both PvP and PvE content.
f40:
A Healer is a player who specializes in restoring health and keeping their group alive during combat.

Healers use a variety of healing spells, buffs, and protective abilities to mend damage taken by teammates and prevent deaths. They must carefully manage their resources and prioritize targets to ensure the group stays alive through challenging encounters. 

In addition to direct healing, Healers often provide utility through removing harmful effects, dispelling debuffs, and offering supportive buffs that enhance the group’s survivability.

f23: Healing power is a secondary stat that increases the effectiveness of your healing spells and abilities.
f40:
Healing power is a secondary stat that increases the effectiveness of your healing spells and abilities. The higher your Healing Power, the more health your abilities restore, making it essential for all healing-focused builds.

You can view your healing power in Character Info (Hotkey C).

f23:
A Hearthstone lets you teleport to your set Inn location and is essential for quick travel, safety, and totem-based abilities. 

It has a 30-minute cooldown, can be replaced for free at any innkeeper, and should always be kept in your inventory.
f40:
A Hearthstone is an item that allows your character to instantly teleport back to the Inn you've set as your current home location. Every player starts with a Hearthstone automatically, bound to their starter zone, and it can be used to quickly return to town for safety, repairs, or quest turn-ins. You can change your home location by speaking with any Innkeeper and selecting the 'Make this Inn your home.' option.

If your Hearthstone is ever lost or deleted, it can be easily replaced by talking to any innkeeper, who will provide a new one at no cost. Hearthstones have a 30 minute cooldown, so they’re best used strategically when fast travel is needed.

In addition to travel, Hearthstones also have a unique purpose as they serve as an all-in-one totem reagent. Totem-based abilities depend on having a hearthstone in your inventory, so it’s important to keep one with you at all times, even if you use alternate travel methods like teleport scrolls or portals.

f23:
Heirlooms are Realm-Bound gear that scales in power as you level and provides bonus Experience. 

Stored in your Vanity Collection, they’re accessible to all your characters on the same realm.
f40:
Heirlooms are special pieces of Realm-Bound gear designed to scale with your character as they level, making them ideal for leveling alternative characters or speeding up the journey to maximum level. These items not only increase in power as your character gains levels, but many also provide bonus Experience, helping you level faster through quests, kills, and battlegrounds.

Heirlooms are stored in your Vanity Collection and are accessible to all characters on the same realm. Once unlocked, you can equip heirlooms on any eligible character, giving you a powerful head start with solid stats and consistent performance across all level ranges.

Most heirlooms come in the form of weapons, armor, and trinkets, and some are themed to match specific class roles, such as Strength-based melee, Intellect-based casters, or Agility-based archers.

Heirlooms can be obtained through various means, including purchasing them from Vendors for PvP Points, Prestige Points, Marks of Ascension, and from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

f23:
Heirlooms are Realm-Bound gear that scales in power as you level and grants bonus Experience. They become accessible once your character reaches Prestige level 1 or higher. 

Stored in your Vanity Collection, Heirlooms can be used by all your characters on the same realm.
f40:
Heirlooms are special pieces of Realm-Bound gear designed to scale with your character as they level, making them ideal for leveling alternative characters or speeding up the journey to maximum level. These items not only increase in power as your character gains levels, but many also provide bonus Experience, helping you level faster through quests, kills, and battlegrounds.

Heirlooms are stored in your Vanity Collection and are accessible to all characters on the same realm. However, characters must have prestiged at least once before they are eligible to equip heirlooms. Once that requirement is met, you can freely use heirlooms on any qualifying character, giving you a powerful head start with solid stats and consistent performance across all level ranges.

Most heirlooms come in the form of weapons, armor, and trinkets, and some are themed to match specific class roles, such as Strength-based melee, Intellect-based casters, or Agility-based archers.

Heirlooms can be obtained through various means, including purchasing them from Vendors for PvP Points, Prestige Points, Marks of Ascension, and from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

f23:
Herbalism is a Primary Profession and a Gathering Profession that gathers various plants from the environment.

Items gathered from Herbalism are primarily used in the Crafting Profession Alchemy.
f40:
Herbalism is a Primary Profession and a Gathering Profession for players who enjoy exploring the open world while collecting natural resources. Herbs gathered by herbalists are used in Crafting Professions like Alchemy.

To get started, you’ll need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn herbalism. Once trained, you can begin gathering herbs by locating plant nodes found throughout the open world. After learning the Profession, you'll also unlock the 'Find Herbs' function in the Map Lens, which highlights nearby herb nodes, making it much easier to spot gathering opportunities as you explore.

Each herb node you gather has a chance to contribute to your herbalism skill and provides plant-based materials used directly in crafting. Different zones contain different types of herbs, typically tied to level ranges and progression, so exploring new areas becomes a rewarding part of leveling the Profession.

While herbalism does not require a special tool to gather herbs, many players combine it with Crafting Professions like Alchemy to streamline their material supply. For those managing multiple professions, investing in an Ethereal Tool Dispenser can be helpful as this item consolidates all Profession tools into a single inventory slot and is available from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP) or from the Auction House for in-game gold.

f23:
The Hero Architect (Hotkey N -> Hero Architect Tab) is a library of featured builds and community created builds. You can use it to discover new archetypes or share your setup with other players. 

Featured builds guarantee a powerful build designed to teach you how to play it effectively.
f40:
The Hero Architect (Hotkey N -> Hero Architect Tab) is a library of featured builds and community created builds that contain full loadouts of spells, Talents, recommended playstyles, macros, equipment suggestions, and various buff recommendations. 

You can use it to discover new archetypes or share your setup with other players. Community builds can be created by anyone, but you can guarantee a powerful build with the 'Featured Builds' category, designed to teach you how to play effectively.

f23:
Heroic dungeons are tougher versions of normal dungeons, designed for maximum level characters. 

Expect stronger enemies, more powerful bosses, and significantly better loot.
f40:
Heroic dungeons are tougher, maximum level versions of regular dungeons, designed to offer greater challenges and significantly improved rewards. These dungeons feature enhanced enemies, harder-hitting bosses, and more complex mechanics, making them a key part of any player’s endgame progression.

To enter a heroic Dungeon from the open world, right-click your character portrait, select 'Dungeon Difficulty', and switch to 'Heroic' before entering the instance. Otherwise simply select the Dungeon you desire from the specific list, or use the 'Random Heroic Dungeon' option from the Dungeon Finder.

Heroic dungeons offer access to endgame PvE currencies. Bosses in these dungeons drop either Marks of Triumph (in Vanilla content) or Badges of Justice (in Burning Crusade content).

These currencies can be exchanged at special vendors in your Capital City or PvE hub for specific pieces of Dungeon-quality gear, giving players a guaranteed path to upgrades even if the boss doesn’t drop what they need directly. This system helps ensure that everyone in the group can make progress.

Heroic dungeons are a core stepping stone into the next Raid, mythic Dungeon, and high-end character builds, offering a reliable way to gear up and master your role.

f23:
This is a ruleset that allows players to engage in open-world PvP and loot gear and items from defeated opponents but risk losing their own if they die. 

Equipment can be protected using Fel Commutation for a price, and looted items become powerful Bloodforged gear.
f40:
High-Risk PvP Mode is a ruleset designed for players seeking a high-stakes, full-loot PvP extravaganza. 

In this mode, defeating other players allows you to loot their gear and inventory, creating intense and rewarding encounters. However, the danger goes both ways, if you die, you risk dropping a piece of your equipped gear, along with items from your bags.

To help manage the risk, players can use Fel Commutation, a system that allows you to protect specific gear pieces from being dropped on death. 

Items that are not protected by Fel Commutation and are looted in High-Risk PvP Mode immediately become Bloodforged with powerful PvP stats.

To enable High-Risk mode, head to your Capital City and open the Hybrid Risk menu (Hotkey H -> PvP Ruleset Tab), then select 'High-Risk PvP Mode' as your active ruleset. Keep in mind that switching between PvP modes has a 15 minute cooldown, so plan your activities accordingly.

f23: The Hit Cap is the minimum Hit Rating needed to ensure your attacks never miss (4% for players, 8% for Raid bosses with physical attacks, and 17% for Raid bosses with spells).
f40:
The Hit Cap refers to the minimum amount of Hit Rating a player needs to never miss an attack on an enemy. Reaching the hit cap ensures your offensive abilities connect reliably, especially in high level content like Dungeons and Raids.

The hit cap is divided into two categories, players and Raid bosses.

To never miss a player with a physical attack or spell, you need 4% Hit Rating.
To never miss a Raid boss with a physical attack, you need 8% Hit Rating.
To never miss a Raid boss with a spell, you need 17% Hit Rating. 

Raid bosses have higher resistance and avoidance, meaning players typically need a higher Hit Cap to perform consistently in endgame content.

If you're at or above the hit cap, any extra Hit Rating provides no additional benefit and could be better spent on other stats like Critical Strike or Haste.

You can find your hit cap by mousing over “Hit Rating” in Character Info (Hotkey C).

f23:
Hit rating is a secondary stat that increases your chance to hit with spells and abilities. 

Melee, ranged, and spells require different amounts of hit to ensure you never miss a target.
f40:
Hit rating is a secondary stat that increases your chance to successfully land spells and abilities on your target. It helps prevent your attacks from missing, which is vital for maintaining a consistent damage output.

Melee, ranged, and spell attacks each have their own Hit Cap. Reaching the appropriate Hit Cap for your build and content type (PvE or PvP) is a key part of optimizing performance.

You can find your current hit rating in Character Info (Hotkey C).

f23:
A Hotspot is a temporary area in the open world that grants bonus Experience for defeating enemies and completing quests. 

Hotspots are announced within their zone when they appear, and you can also spot them on the World Map while you’re in that specific zone.
f40:
A Hotspot is a temporary, rotating area in the open world that offers a bonus to Experience gained from defeating enemies and completing quests within its boundaries.

When a hotspot becomes active, it’s announced in the chat for players currently in that zone, making it easy to know when and where one has appeared. You can also identify a Hotspot by looking at your World Map (if you’re in the affected zone).

Hotspots rotate periodically and can appear in different zones, encouraging players to move around the world and take advantage of shifting leveling opportunities.

f23:
Honor Points are gained through various PvP activities. 

Stored in the Currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab), Honor Points can be used to purchase gear, mounts, and other items at a PvP Quartermaster.
f40:
Honor Points are the main PvP Currency earned by participating in Player vs. Player activities. You can gain Honor by fighting in battlegrounds, engaging in open world PvP, completing PvP daily quests, and participating in PvP events. The more you contribute to defeating enemy players and completing objectives, the more Honor you’ll earn.

Your current total is stored in the Currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab).

Honor Points can be spent at PvP Quartermasters, who offer a wide variety of PvP-focused rewards, including seasonal gear, weapons, Mounts, cosmetic items, and other useful tools for both combat and style.

f23:
PvP Quartermasters sell seasonal PvP gear for Honor Points and Arena Points. 

These NPCs are located in Capital Cities or PvP hubs and can be found by asking a city guard or searching for the PvP icon on the World Map.
f40:
A PvP Quartermaster is a vendor who sells rare and epic Quality PvP gear, available in exchange for Honor Points and Arena Points. These Vendors are your main source of PvP equipment outside of Bloodforged gear.

PvP Quartermasters are typically found in Capital Cities and PvP-focused hubs throughout the world. To locate them easily, look for the PvP icon on the World Map or ask a guard.

The gear sold by these quartermasters is seasonal, meaning it changes with each competitive PvP season to reflect updated balance and rewards.

f23:
Ascension features a hybrid risk PvP system, letting players choose their preferred PvP ruleset. 

You can opt for PvE Mode, No-Risk PvP Mode, or High-Risk PvP Mode depending on your playstyle.
f40:
Ascension features a unique hybrid-risk PvP system that gives players full control over how they engage with enemy players in combat. Instead of locking everyone into a single PvP ruleset, you can choose from three distinct modes (PvE Mode, No-Risk PvP Mode, and High-Risk PvP Mode) each offering a different level of intensity, danger, and reward. 

This system ensures that players with different goals and playstyles can coexist in the same world while enjoying the game on their own terms.

PvE Mode and No-Risk PvP Mode players share the same game world, meaning both PvE and PvP players can interact with the environment and each other (within their ruleset boundaries) without being forced into unwanted combat.

To select your PvP ruleset, visit your Capital City and open the hybrid risk menu (Hotkey H -> PvP Ruleset Tab), then choose the mode that best fits your current gameplay goals. Keep in mind that switching between PvP modes has a 15 minute cooldown, so plan your activities accordingly.

f23:
Most quest hubs and cities feature an inn, where players can find innkeepers to set their Hearthstone teleport location. 

Logging out inside an inn grants you Rested Experience.
f40:
Inns are important locations found in most quest hubs, towns, and cities throughout the world. Each inn is managed by an innkeeper, who can function as a vendor and bind your Hearthstone to their location.

To bind your Hearthstone, speak to the Innkeeper and select the option to 'Make this Inn your home.' Upon its next use, your Hearthstone will teleport you back to that location.

Inns also serve as rest areas, meaning if you log out inside an inn, you’ll gradually accumulate Rested Experience. Spending even a few hours offline in an inn can provide a significant Experience boost, making them valuable for both active and casual players.

To quickly find an inn or innkeeper in any area, use the Map Lens and select 'Innkeeper' to highlight any nearby Inns.

f23:
Intellect is the Primary Attribute for those who wield the power of magic, channeling knowledge into devastating spells and potent utility. 

It’s an excellent stat for casters who focus on ranged spell damage.
f40:
Intellect is the Primary Attribute that represents mental acuity, magical knowledge, and the ability to harness arcane, divine, or elemental forces. It is a core stat for players who specialize in spellcasting, making it vital for dealing magic damage, healing allies, or using utility spells effectively.

Effects of intellect:

+1 Intellect increases your maximum Mana by 15.
+1 Intellect increases your Spell and Melee Critical Strike Rating.

Intellect also affects Mana Regeneration indirectly, especially when paired with Spirit or talents that scale from intellect.

f23:
Jewelcrafting is a Primary Profession and a Crafting Profession that creates jewelry, trinkets, and gems to enhance your equipment.

Jewelcrafting is reliant on Mining for materials.
f40:
Jewelcrafting is a Primary Profession and a Crafting Profession that is only available in Burning Crusade content and beyond.

Jewelcrafting focuses on cutting gems and crafting jewelry to enhance gear with powerful stat bonuses. Jewelcrafters can create rings, necklaces, trinkets, and cut gems used in sockets.

To begin, you’ll need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn jewelcrafting. Once trained, you can start collecting or purchasing the necessary materials, primarily being raw gems and ores gathered through Mining.

As you level up, you’ll unlock Recipes, known as designs, that teach you how to cut specific gems and craft a variety of jewelry.

Creating most jewelcrafting items requires a jeweler’s kit, which must be in your inventory while crafting. For those managing multiple professions, investing in an Ethereal Tool Dispenser can be helpful as this item consolidates all Profession tools into a single inventory slot and is available from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP) or from the Auction House for in-game gold.

f23:
Leatherworking is a Primary Profession and a Crafting Profession that creates leather and mail equipment, armor kits, and various utility items.

Leatherworking is reliant on Skinning for materials.
f40:
Leatherworking is a Primary Profession and a Crafting Profession focused on turning hides and leathers gathered from beasts into a variety of practical items such as equipment and stat-boosting armor kits. Leatherworkers create essential gear for leather and mail wearers, as well as niche items that are required through specific endgame content.

To begin, you’ll need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn leatherworking. Once trained, you can start collecting or purchasing the necessary materials. Leatherworking relies primarily on hides and leathers obtained by Skinning throughout the open world, which can then be processed into tougher materials used in crafting.

As you level up, you’ll unlock Recipes, known as patterns, that teach you how to craft specific armor pieces and useful gear enhancements. Leatherworkers can also create specialized items like armor kits that provide armor buffs, small Bags, toys, and unique gear that is required in various end-game content.

While Leatherworking does not need specific tools to craft, many players pair it with Skinning to streamline their material gathering. For those managing multiple professions, investing in an Ethereal Tool Dispenser can be helpful as this item consolidates all Profession tools into a single inventory slot and is available from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP) or from the Auction House for in-game gold.

f23:
Players can equip one legendary enchant in their Active Enchant Slots at a time. 

These mystic enchants provide powerful, build-defining bonuses and unlock unique spells that open up entirely new playstyles!
f40:
A legendary enchant is a powerful type of Mystic Enchant that serves as the centerpiece of most custom builds. Unlike rare or epic enchants, legendary enchants offer game-changing effects, often unlocking entirely new spells, mechanics, or class-defining abilities that can drastically enhance your character’s playstyle.

Players can equip one legendary enchant at a time in their Active Enchant Slots. Because of their power and uniqueness, choosing a legendary enchant is often the first step in crafting a build, as the rest of your enchants, Talents, and abilities are typically selected to support and enhance it.

Legendary enchants range from thematic class hybrids (like combining elemental magic with rogue techniques) to completely original effects, using new resource systems, or transforming spells into entirely new abilities. Many popular builds are centered around these enchants, making them a core part of character identity and progression.

Legendary enchants can be found through various means, including reforging Mystic Scrolls, discovering them as a Worldforged Mystic Enchant, or purchasing them off of the Auction House from other players.

f23: Looking For Group, or LFG, is a common phrase used by solo players seeking a group of other people to join for Dungeons, Raids, or quests.
f40:
LFG, short for 'Looking For Group', is a common term used by players who are seeking others to join them in multiplayer content such as Dungeons, Raids, world bosses, or group quests. If you're playing solo but want to take on group-based challenges, typing 'LFG' in chat (often followed by the name or level of the activity, like 'LFG 70 Dungeons' is the standard way to signal that you're available and ready to team up.

The opposite of this is LFM, or 'Looking For Member', which is used when a player or group already has a party started and is recruiting others to fill specific roles, such as a tank, healer, or DPS. For example, someone might post 'LFM Tank and Heals for mythic+' if they already have damage dealers and need the remaining roles.

f23:
Intellect is the Primary Attribute for those who wield the power of magic, channeling knowledge into devastating spells and potent utility. 

It’s an excellent stat for casters who focus on ranged spell damage.
f40:
Intellect is the Primary Attribute for those who wield the power of magic, channeling knowledge into devastating spells and potent utility. It’s an excellent stat for casters who focus on ranged spell damage.
Choosing the Path of Arcana makes Intellect your main stat, greatly enhancing your magical effectiveness. 

You gain bonus Spell Power, Intellect, and Spirit, improving both your offensive and regenerative capabilities. On top of that, all Spell Power gains are doubled, giving a significant boost to every spell you cast.

The Path of Arcana also grants two powerful passive abilities, depending on your weapon choice:

Magic Acceleration: When wielding a two-handed weapon, your spell Haste is increased by 12%, allowing for faster casting and smoother spell rotations.

Devastating Spells: When using a one-handed weapon, your spell damage is increased by 5%, amplifying your spell output and making each cast hit harder.

f23:
Each time you complete a new Manastorm level, you earn a Manastorm Cache, with a chance to receive a Bonus Manastorm Cache containing powerful gear. 

The higher the Manastorm level, the better the rewards.
f40:
Manastorm Caches are one of the primary sources of rewards in the Manastorm, offering level-scaled equipment scaled to your current progression. As you delve deeper, the quality of the loot improves (ranging from rare Dungeon gear to epic Raid items from previous tiers) making them especially valuable for solo players or off-meta builds that may struggle in traditional group content. 

You earn a cache each time you complete a new level, ensuring a steady stream of useful upgrades. 

Additionally, there's a chance to receive a Bonus Manastorm Cache, which contain even more loot. The probability to receive a bonus cache increases with Manastorm progression. Bonus caches can also drop during re-clears of previously completed floors, giving players a reason to return even after hitting progression milestones.

f23:
The Manastorm is a randomized, endless dungeon that can be tackled solo or with a group of up to 15 players. 

Discover unique bosses, custom encounters, and more difficult enemies as you progress deeper into the Manastorm.
f40:
The Manastorm is a dynamic, randomized, and endlessly scaling dungeon challenge, designed to test your skills, creativity, and survivability. It can be tackled solo or with a raid group of up to 15 players, offering flexible difficulty and a wide range of rewards.

Each run of the Manastorm is procedurally generated, featuring unique bosses, custom encounters, randomized layouts, and increasingly difficult enemies the deeper you progress. As you ascend, you’ll encounter environmental hazards, elite foes, and powerful modifiers that keep every floor engaging and unpredictable.

Successful progression through the Manastorm earns you a variety of valuable rewards, including Manastorm Caches, Bedlam Bullions, Bonzo Bolts, gold, Experience, and more.

If your group is defeated, you'll be ejected from the Manastorm and must start a new ascent. However, progress saves every 5 floors, so you can resume climbing later without starting over entirely.

Upon exiting (whether voluntarily or by defeat) you’ll be automatically teleported back to your Capital City, where you’ll appear right next to Millhouse Manastorm. From there, you can immediately spend your earned currency on rewards and prepare for your next dive into the arcane storm.

f23:
The Map Lens is the magnifying glass icon on your mini-map. 

It’s a search tool that highlights nearby NPCs or key locations with golden dots, making it easier to find Vendors, trainers, innkeepers, and more.
f40:
The Map Lens is the magnifying glass icon located on your mini-map, acting as a search and filtering tool for navigating the world around you. When clicked, the map lens opens a menu that allows you to highlight specific types of NPCs and key locations in your immediate area such as repair NPCs, Vendors, trainers, innkeepers, bankers, and more.

In addition to tracking NPCs, the Map Lens is also where you can enable tracking for a Gathering Profession. This functionality is essential for efficiently farming resources in the world and leveling up your gathering skills.

Once you select what you are searching for, the NPCs or gathering nodes will appear as golden dots on your mini-map, making it much easier to locate important services and items, especially in busy Capital Cities or new zones.

f23: Upon entering the Manastorm, each player receives Millhouse’s Magical Escape - a reusable, short-cooldown item that breaks crowd control and movement impairing effects on your character.
f40:
Millhouse’s Magical Escape is a reusable, utility item placed in every player’s inventory upon entering the Manastorm. This enchanted gadget serves as a lifeline during high-stress encounters, allowing you to instantly break free from crowd control (CC) and Movement Impairing effects with the push of a button.

With a short cooldown and no resource cost, Millhouse’s Magical Escape is essential for surviving the Manastorm’s fast-paced, unpredictable challenges. Many of the Manastorm’s enemies and environmental hazards are designed to lock you down or trap you in damaging mechanics and this item gives you a reliable way out. Whether you’re stunned, rooted, or slowed, it can provide the split-second freedom needed to reposition, dodge lethal mechanics, or finish off a tricky boss.

While it’s only usable inside the Manastorm instance, Millhouse’s Magical Escape is one of the most important tools at your disposal so be sure to drag it to your action bar and keep it within easy reach.

f23: Millhouse Manastorm is a quirky and well-loved gnome who guides you through the Manastorm and trades Bedlam Bullions for a variety of cosmetic and convenience items.
f40:
Millhouse Manastorm is a quirky and beloved gnome NPC who serves as your guide through the Manastorm and Vendor for Bedlam Bullions. He offers a wide selection of cosmetic items, convenience tools, and hilarious toys, making him a key figure for players looking to personalize their experience or gain quality-of-life upgrades.

Whenever you exit the Manastorm you will be automatically teleported to Millhouse’s location at the entrance of your Capital City. There, you can immediately spend your hard-earned currency on unique rewards.

f23:
Mining is a Primary Profession and a Gathering Profession that gathers ore, stones, and gems from mineral nodes using a pickaxe.

Items gathered from Mining are used in the Crafting Professions Blacksmithing, Engineering, and Jewelcrafting.
f40:
Mining is a Primary Profession and a Gathering Profession for players who enjoy exploring the open world while collecting natural resources. Materials gathered by miners are used in a Crafting Profession like Engineering or Blacksmithing.

To get started, you’ll need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn mining. Once trained, you can begin gathering materials by locating mineral nodes found throughout the open world. After learning the profession, you'll also unlock the 'Find Minerals' function in the Map Lens, which highlights nearby ore nodes, making it much easier to spot gathering opportunities as you explore.

Each mineral node you gather has a chance to contribute to your mining skill and provides stone-based materials used directly in crafting. Different zones contain different types of minerals, typically tied to level ranges and progression, so exploring new areas becomes a rewarding part of leveling the Profession.

To harvest minerals, you’ll need a pickaxe, which can be purchased from Vendors. This tool must be in your inventory while gathering and is essential for collecting ore. For those managing multiple professions, investing in an Ethereal Tool Dispenser can be helpful as this item consolidates all Profession tools into a single inventory slot and is available from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP) or from the Auction House for in-game gold.

f23: A mount is a player-controlled ride used to travel faster across the world—but only outdoors.
f40:
A mount is a player-controlled creature that boosts movement speed for faster travel. Found in the Pets Tab (Hotkey Shift + P), mounts are vital for leveling, exploration, and convenience, and come in various cosmetic styles and types. The various mount types provide unique advantages based on the terrain.

Ground Mounts:
Unlocked first, these mounts increase movement speed by 40%, with higher speeds available from Riding Trainers. Usable only outdoors, they dismount you in buildings, or when using certain abilities. All mounts can function as ground mounts, regardless of type.

Flying Mounts:
These mounts enable aerial travel in zones that support it (Outland and Northrend). Flying mounts require flight training and the proper zone; otherwise, they act as ground mounts.

Aquatic Mounts:
Designed for swimming, these mounts boost swim speed but offer little to no speed on land. Ideal for underwater activities, these rare mounts offer unique utility.

Mounts can be obtained through quests, achievements, Vendors, the Auction House, seasonal events, or purchased from the Ascension Store.

f23: Mana regeneration (also known as MP5 or mana per 5) is a secondary stat that increases the amount of mana you restore every 5 seconds, even while in combat.
f40:
Mana Regeneration (also known as MP5 or mana per 5) is a secondary stat that increases the amount of mana you restore every 5 seconds, even while in combat. This helps sustain your ability usage during longer fights, especially for casters and hybrid builds that rely heavily on mana.

You can view your current mana regeneration rate in Character Info (Hotkey C).

f23: A Mystic Enchanting: Specialization scroll is a consumable item that unlocks an additional enchant specialization slot for the character it's used on.
f40:
A Mystic Enchanting: Specialization scroll is a powerful consumable item that unlocks an additional Mystic Enchant Specialization slot for the character it's used on. 

With enough scrolls, you can unlock up to 12 Mystic Enchant specializations. This gives you the freedom to experiment with a variety of enchant combinations without needing to manually reapply them each time you want to change your setup.

There are several ways to obtain a Specialization scroll. You can purchase one from the Auction House or Tiraxis for in-game currency, or from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

f23:
Mystic Enchanting is a powerful system that lets you customize your character using Mystic Scrolls. 

These enchants can enhance abilities, unlock new spells, and have the potential to completely change how you play.
f40:
Mystic Enchanting is a core customization system that allows players to personalize their characters by applying a Mystic Enchant. These enchants can drastically change how your character functions, offering both subtle stat boosts and game-changing mechanics like new spells, altered abilities, or entirely new playstyles.

Mystic enchants can either be rare or uncommon quality, which can be used to enhance your stats and abilities that you already know.

To access your enchants, open the mystic enchanting menu (Hotkey N -> Mystic Enchant Tab). In this panel, you can equip and manage your Active Enchant Slots, view your Mystic Enchant Collection, and browse for new powers by quality. You can also reforge or extract new enchants using Mystic Scrolls.

f23:
Worldforged Mystic Enchants are unique enchants that can only be discovered, they cannot be traded, bought, or Reforged. 

Find them by defeating bosses, solving puzzles, and exploring hidden areas.
f40:
Worldforged Mystic Enchants are a special category of powerful enchants that can only be discovered through exploration, combat, and solving in-game challenges. Unlike regular mystic enchants, worldforged enchants cannot be traded, purchased, or reforged from regular Mystic Scrolls, they must be found in the world and unlocked through gameplay.

These enchants are hidden across the open world and are often obtained by defeating specific bosses, solving puzzles, interacting with secret objects, or exploring hidden areas.

To track your progress, open the Mystic Enchant menu (Hotkey N -> Mystic Enchant Tab) and filter your collection by 'Not Collected -> Worldforged Enchants'. Hovering over any locked enchant in this list will give you a lore-friendly hint or clue guiding you to its location.

f23:
Worldforged Mystic Scrolls are Soulbound items dropped by specific enemy types and come in eight varieties, each looted from a different enemy category. 

Using a scroll grants a random enchant for one of your known abilities that matches the scroll’s type, enhancing your powers, but it cannot be traded or reforged.
f40:
A Worldforged Mystic Scroll is a Soulbound scroll that contains a unique Worldforged Mystic Enchant. Unlike regular Mystic Scrolls, these cannot be traded, purchased, or reforged, making them a rare and valuable source of specialized enchantments.

Worldforged Mystic Scrolls come in eight distinct types (Fighter, Wizard, Primal, Demonic, Draconic, Gigantic, Necrotic, and Element-Bound) each associated with a specific enemy type that drops them. This categorization ties the scrolls closely to the world’s lore and enemies, encouraging players to hunt particular creatures to find them.

When you use a worldforged scroll, it grants a random enchant for one of your known abilities that matches the scroll’s type. These enchants specifically enhance your existing abilities, offering powerful and often unique bonuses tailored to the corresponding theme.

f23:
Mystic Enchanting is a powerful system that lets you customize your character using Mystic Scrolls. 

These enchants can enhance abilities, unlock new spells, and have the potential to completely change how you play.
f40:
Mystic Enchanting is a core customization system that allows players to personalize their characters by applying a Mystic Enchant. These enchants can drastically change how your character functions, offering both subtle stat boosts and game-changing mechanics like new spells, altered abilities, or entirely new playstyles.

Mystic enchants are divided into four main tiers and each slot requires an enchant that matches its quality.

Rare (6 slots): Enhances abilities you already know.
Epic (3 slots): Introduces new spells or creatively reimagines existing abilities.
Legendary (1 slot): Grants a powerful new ability or passive that alters your playstyle.
Artifact (1 slot): Unlocks a new spell focused on movement, defense, or crowd control.

To access your enchants, open the mystic enchanting menu (Hotkey N -> Mystic Enchant Tab). In this panel, you can equip and manage your Active Enchant Slots, view your Mystic Enchant Collection, and browse for new powers by quality. You can also reforge or extract new enchants using Mystic Scrolls.

f23:

You can obtain them by reforging Tarnished Mystic Scrolls at an Enchanting Altar, defeating specific enemies, looting hidden objects, or completing special quests.
f40:
Mystic Enchants are unique and powerful enhancements that allow you to customize and empower your character beyond traditional abilities. They can significantly alter your playstyle by granting new effects, improving your damage, survivability, utility, or even unlocking entirely new mechanics.

You can obtain these enchants when you reforge Mystic Scrolls at an Enchanting Altar, by defeating specific enemies or bosses, by looting hidden objects scattered throughout the world, and by completing special quests.

Once obtained, enchants can be applied by consuming Mystic Scrolls or saved permanently in your Mystic Enchant Collection using a Mystic Extract.

f23:
A Mystic Scroll contains a powerful Mystic Enchant and, when used, will enhance your character.

You can either consume the scroll to apply its effects immediately, reforge it into a new scroll at an Enchanting Altar, or save it to your Mystic Enchant Collection using a Mystic Extract for later use.
f40:
A Mystic Scroll is an item that contains a powerful Mystic Enchant, which can enhance your character’s abilities and playstyle. These scrolls serve as the primary way to obtain new enchants and experiment with different build options.

You can apply a mystic scroll directly to one of your Active Enchant Slots at any time without needing an Enchanting Altar. Doing so immediately grants the enchant’s benefits but consumes the scroll, so it’s a one-time use unless you acquire another copy.

If you want to keep the enchant permanently for future use, you can take the scroll to an Enchanting Altar and use a Mystic Extract to save it into your Mystic Enchant Collection. This allows you to apply the saved enchant repeatedly for Mystic Orbs, without using up more scrolls.

Alternatively, you can reforge your mystic scroll at an Enchanting Altar using Mystic Runes to transform the scroll into a different, randomly selected enchant. This system system lets you learn undiscovered enchants or try new effects without needing to find or buy new scrolls.

Mystic Extracts are a Currency (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab) used to save a Mystic Scroll’s enchant permanently into your Enchant Collection. 

You earn a Mystic Extract with every Mystic Enchant Level or by purchasing a Mystic Draught.
f40:
Mystic Extracts are a Currency used to permanently save Mystic Enchants from Mystic Scrolls into your Mystic Enchant Collection. Once an enchant is extracted and added to your collection, you can freely apply it to your character’s Active Enchant Slots using Mystic Orbs, without needing to rely on scrolls or reforging again. You can view your Mystic Extracts in the Currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab).

You earn 1 mystic extract every time you gain a Mystic Enchanting Level, which happens as you continue to reforge Mystic Scrolls at an Enchanting Altar. Each new level reflects your progress and familiarity with the enchantment system and rewards you with another Extract to use.

In addition to leveling up through reforging, you can also gain Mystic Extracts by using a Mystic Draught, an item available from various in-game Vendors. These draughts provide an instant extract and are a great option for players who want to speed up their collection progress or focus on unlocking specific enchants more quickly.

f23:
Mystic Runes are a currency (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab) used to Reforge Mystic Scrolls at an Enchanting Altar. 

They can be earned through various types of content, and especially the Call Board Daily Quest.
f40:
Mystic Runes are a Currency used to reforge Mystic Scrolls at an Enchanting Altar, allowing you to roll for new mystic enchants. This is a key part of the mystic enchantment system, giving you a way to discover specific enchants or try your luck with random ones. You can view your Mystic Runes in the Currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab).

Reforging a scroll costs runes and gives you a new, randomly selected Mystic Enchant on that scroll. This mechanic is essential for players looking to complete their Enchant Collection or perfect a build.

Mystic runes can be earned through a variety of in-game activities, including PvE, PvP, and most reliably through the Call Board Daily Quest.

f23:
Mystic Orbs are a Currency (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab) used to apply a Mystic Enchant from your Mystic Enchant Collection to your Active Enchant Slots. 

They can be earned through various types of content, and especially the Call Board Daily Quest.
f40:
Mystic Orbs are a Currency used to apply a Mystic Enchant from your Mystic Enchant Collection to your character's Active Enchant Slots. These orbs are a key part of customizing your build, letting you add powerful effects to your gear that define or enhance your playstyle. You can view your mystic orbs in the Currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab).

Orbs are required any time you want to assign a Mystic Enchant from your Mystic Enchant Collection to one of your available slots.

Mystic Orbs can be earned through a variety of in-game activities, including PvE, PvP, and most reliably through the Call Board Daily Quest.

f23:
Mythic+ dungeons are timed, repeatable challenges that scale in difficulty based on your mythic keystone level, adding affixes that change weekly to keep gameplay dynamic. 

Completing runs quickly upgrades your key and boosts rewards, offering some of the best gear and progression in PvE content.
f40:
Mythic+ dungeons are a high-level, repeatable challenge mode designed to test your skill, coordination, and efficiency. To begin a mythic+ run, you’ll need a mythic keystone, which you earn by completing a Dungeon at mythic difficulty. Once you have a key, you can activate it at the dungeon’s entrance to begin the run.

Unlike standard mythics, mythic+ dungeons are timed and scale in difficulty based on the level of your keystone. As the keystone level increases, enemies become stronger, and affixes (special dungeon modifiers) are added that introduce new mechanics such as environmental hazards, enemy buffs, or group-wide pressure. These affixes change weekly and vary depending on the key level, keeping runs fresh and challenging.

At the end of each run, your keystone transforms based on your performance, either increasing in level or changing to a different dungeon. Completing the dungeon quickly can upgrade your key and increase your rewards, while failing to complete within the timer may lower the difficulty.

Higher level mythic+ runs offer increasingly better rewards, including epic gear, Currency, and progression toward achievements and leaderboards.

f23: No-risk PvP mode is a ruleset that allows players to engage in open-world PvP without any penalty for death.
f40:
No-risk PvP mode is a ruleset that allows players to participate in open-world PvP without the danger of losing gear or items upon death. 

This makes it a great choice for players who enjoy PvP combat but prefer a lower-stakes environment. In no-risk PvP mode, you can freely attack and be attacked by other players who are also flagged for PvP while still keeping your inventory, gear, and gold completely safe if you’re defeated.

The no-risk world is shared with PvE mode players, meaning both groups exist in the same zones. However, you cannot attack or be attacked by players in PvE Mode. This shared environment creates a dynamic world where PvP and PvE players can coexist without conflict.

To enable no-risk PvP mode, head to your Capital City and open the Hybrid Risk menu (Hotkey H -> PvP Ruleset Tab), then select 'No-Risk PvP Mode' as your active ruleset. Keep in mind that switching between PvP modes has a 15 minute cooldown, so plan your activities accordingly.

f23:
The Options Menu lets you customize your gameplay, including controls, graphics, sound, and interface settings. 

Accessible via the Esc Key or clicking the “?” in the Micro Menu, it also offers tools for UI tweaks, character-specific preferences, and support features like bug reporting.
f40:
The Options Menu is your central hub for customizing your gameplay experience. You can open it by pressing the Escape (Esc) key or by clicking the red (?) icon located in the micro menu at the bottom of your screen. From here, you can adjust a wide range of settings to fine-tune how the game looks, sounds, and feels.

Within the Options Menu, you’ll find tabs for keybindings, graphics, sound, and interface settings. You can remap your keys for more comfortable controls, optimize your graphics settings for better performance or visual quality, and adjust sound effects or music volume to your liking. It also includes features for UI customization, such as toggling floating combat text, adjusting display options, and enabling auto-loot.

Under the Interface tab, you’ll find character-specific settings like the option to hide your helmet or cloak, adjust camera behavior, or modify action bar layouts. These options help you tailor the game's interface and visuals to match your preferences and playstyle.

Additionally, the options menu provides tools for reporting bugs or contacting the Ascension team if you encounter technical issues or need support. It's an essential tool not only for improving your gameplay but also for communicating with the developers when needed.

f23: Orgrimmar (Org) is the fierce and fortified Capital City of the Horde located in the harsh region of Durotar.
f40:
Orgrimmar (Org) is the fierce and fortified Capital City of the Horde faction, located in the harsh, arid region of Durotar. It serves as the central hub where Horde players can find key NPCs, Vendors, Class Trainers, and Quest Givers.

As the heart of Horde civilization, Orgrimmar is known for its rugged, tribal architecture built from massive stone and wood, reflecting the strength and resilience of its inhabitants. The city is named after Orgrim Doomhammer, a legendary orc warrior.

Orgrimmar is divided into several districts such as the Valley of Strength, home to the Bank and Auction House; the Drag, where you’ll find Profession Trainers, craftsmen, and Vendors; and the Cleft of Shadow, the center for dark magic and other covert activities.

Orgrimmar is a fortress against both monstrous threats and enemy players, providing a safe place for Horde adventurers to rest, craft, trade, and organize before heading out to explore or battle across Azeroth.

f23: Parry is a secondary stat that increases your chance to deflect and avoid melee damage from enemies in front of you or to your sides, but it doesn't work against attacks from behind.
f40:
Parry is a secondary stat that increases your chance to deflect and avoid melee attacks from enemies positioned in front of you or to your sides. However, it does not provide any benefit against attacks coming from behind.

You can find your current parry rating in Character Info (Hotkey C).

f23:
A party is a group of 2 to 5 players who team up to complete content together. 

A typical party usually includes 1 Tank, 1 Healer, and 3 DPS players.
f40:
A party is a small group of 2 to 5 players who team up to complete content together. Parties are used for a wide range of cooperative activities, including questing, dungeons, elite mobs, and PvP battlegrounds. Playing in a party allows you to share Experience, complete group objectives more easily, and support one another with different roles and abilities.

To form a party, right-click on another player’s portrait and select 'Invite', or type '/invite PlayerName' in the chat box. Once invited, the other player can accept to join your group. To leave a party, you can either type '/leave' or right-click your own portrait and select 'Leave Party.'

The player who forms a party becomes the Party Leader, marked by a crown icon. The leader can set instance difficulty, queue the group for dungeons or battlegrounds, manage loot rules, and place visible-only-to-party markers on players or enemies. Leadership can be transferred by right-clicking a member’s portrait and selecting ""Promote to Leader.""

A standard party for group content (especially for dungeons) typically includes 1 Tank, 1 Healer, and 3 DPS. This balanced setup ensures your team can handle incoming damage, stay healed, and deal enough damage to defeat enemies efficiently.

f23:
Talent Essences are a resource that allows you to unlock talent nodes, giving you the freedom to customize your character’s abilities beyond your base power. 

Starting at level 10, you earn one talent essence with each level gained.
f40:
Talent Essences are a resource used to unlock talent nodes in the custom talent system. They give you the freedom to customize your character’s power, passives, and unique playstyle far beyond your core abilities.

Starting at level 10, your character earns 1 talent essence per level, allowing for steady advancement as you gain experience. These essences are spent to activate nodes within Character Advancement (Hotkey N), unlocking a wide variety of bonuses such as increased damage, defensive boosts, utility enhancements, or synergy effects for specific builds.

If you want to refund your talent essences and change builds, you will need a Scroll of Talent Unlearning.

As your pet levels up, you earn points to unlock and upgrade abilities, allowing for customized performance in tanking, damage, or utility.
f40:
Pet Talents allow you to specialize your Tamed Beast into one of three distinct roles: tenacity, ferocity, or cunning, based on the type of creature you've tamed. Each pet type is naturally aligned with one of these specializations, and that choice determines which talent tree your pet will use.

Each Specialization has its own unique tree, much like your character’s, where you can spend points to improve your pet’s performance in combat. As your pet levels up, it gains talent points that you can invest in the tree. You’ll need to spend 3 points in a row to unlock the next tier, with more powerful and specialized Talents appearing further down.

To access your pet’s talent tree, right-click on your pet’s portrait and select 'Pet Talents'. From there, you can allocate, review, or reset your pet’s Talents at any time.

f23: Prestige resets your active Wildcard Specialization to level 1 so you can reroll that build while keeping long-term character progress and earning additional rewards.
f40: Prestige lets you return your active Specialization to level 1 and reroll that build from the beginning. Only the active Specialization is rerolled; your other Specializations remain intact, but are locked until you reach max level again. You keep long-term character progress such as professions, gear, Marks of Ascension, currencies, Riding Trainer, and items. Each Prestige increases the bonus Scrolls of Fortune you can earn when reaching max level, and you can buy back Scrolls of Fortune earned from Cases of Fortune so your previous farming still matters. To Prestige, visit Chromie near the Call Board in your faction Capital City.

f23: Prestige allows you to reset all your Talents and abilities back to level 1, effectively rebuilding your character and giving you the opportunity to embark on your leveling journey again while earning exclusive rewards.
f40:
Prestige is a feature that allows you to reset your character back to level 1, wiping all learned abilities and talents while retaining your gear, gold, Mounts, as well as your Reputation standings, Profession levels, and gathered Currency. This system is designed to let you rebuild your character from scratch, offering a fresh leveling experience and the opportunity to experiment with new builds or refine old ones. 

Prestiging offers exclusive rewards like titles, cosmetics, and other unlockables, depending on the realm or seasonal content. 

To Prestige, visit Chromie near the Call Board in your faction’s Capital City.

These stats directly influence your damage, healing, resource regeneration, and survivability, prioritize the attribute that’s best for your playstyle.
f40:
Primary Attributes (also called primary stats) define your character’s power and play a major role in how effective you are in combat. These stats directly influence your damage, healing, resource regeneration, and survivability depending on your class and role.

The primary attributes are:

Strength – Increases melee attack power and is the primary stat for tanks and melee fighters.

Agility – Increases ranged and melee attack power, critical strike chance, dodge, and is the primary stat for ranged characters and agile classes.

Intellect – Increases mana pool and spell Critical Strike chance and is the primary stat for spell casters and healers.

Spirit – Enhances mana regeneration and is a beneficial stat for most healing classes.

Stamina – Increases health and improves survivability across all roles.

Your class will naturally benefit most from specific stats, and your gear will typically prioritize the attributes that best suit your role—whether that’s tanking, healing, melee, or ranged DPS.

f23:
