f40:
Primary Attributes (also known as primary stats) define your character’s power and heavily influence your combat style and effectiveness. Select your primary attribute in the Character Advancement menu (Hotkey N), allowing you to develop your chosen playstyle.

Each primary attribute grants scaling bonuses to abilities, increasing your damage, healing, or utility based on your specialization.

Strength – Unleash powerful, crushing blows on the Path of Might. Ideal for melee fighters and physical damage bruisers.

Agility – Strike fast and true with critical precision on the Path of Finesse. Ideal for archers and nimble fighters.

Intellect – Wield arcane might and amplify your spells on the Path of Arcana. Ideal for spellcasters.

Spirit – Restore and protect your allies through the Path of Mending. Ideal for healers and support casters.

Your chosen primary attribute boosts key stats and directly affects the performance of many abilities, so select the one that best matches your build and goals!

f23:
Profession Specializations are permanent upgrades in a Crafting Profession that unlock unique Recipes and bonuses, earned by completing specific challenges. 

Choose wisely, as switching requires relearning the entire Profession.
f40:
Profession Specializations are advanced branches within a Crafting Profession that allow players to unlock unique Recipes not available to others. Specializations give your Profession a focused identity, whether it’s crafting stronger equipment, more efficient potions, or powerful enhancements, and can greatly enhance your crafting potential. Not all skills have a Profession Specialization, but those that do often offer a meaningful choice that sets your character apart in terms of what you can create and contribute.

To unlock a Profession Specialization, you’ll need to complete a series of tasks that demonstrate your dedication and skill. These challenges vary by Profession and may include completing special quests, crafting high-level items, or building rapport with key NPCs who serve as gatekeepers to the Specialization.

Once selected, your Specialization is permanent and you cannot switch without unlearning the entire Profession and starting over from scratch. This means you’ll lose all progress and Recipes tied to that Profession, so be sure to choose your Specialization carefully based on your goals, playstyle, or market demand.

f23:
Profession Trainers are NPCs who can teach you the skills needed to begin and advance in a Profession. 

Traditional trainers specialize in only one Profession, but the Book of Artisans functions as an all-in-one trainer.
f40:
A Profession Trainer is an NPCs who teach your character the skills needed to learn, level, and specialize in professions. Unlike the Book of Artisans, which serves as an all-in-one training interface, traditional trainers specialize in a single Profession at a time. 

Whether you’re picking up a Primary Profession or a Secondary Skill, trainers are essential for unlocking new Recipes, higher ranks, and Profession Specializations.

Trainers are commonly found in your Capital City, but can also be seen in major towns, and themed areas such as a forge or potion shop. Higher level trainers can be found in more remote or faction-specific zones, and may only become accessible at certain levels or Reputation thresholds.

To make locating trainers easier, you can use the Map Lens to highlight nearby Profession trainers on your mini-map, helping you quickly find the one you need while exploring the world.

f23:
Specializations define the core theme or playstyle of your build in a classless system, offering identity without limiting creativity. 

With a Tome of Specialization, you can unlock and switch between multiple builds on the same character.
f40:
Specializations (or Spec) in a classless setting, represents the core identity or focus of your build. While you’re free to combine any abilities, a Specialization helps define the main theme or purpose of your build. 

Your Specialization is a general label for the type of gameplay you're aiming for, even if your build doesn’t fully match traditional expectations. It gives your character a recognizable identity without limiting your creative freedom.

With a Tome of Specialization, you can unlock multiple Specialization loadouts, giving you the flexibility to create and swap between different builds on the same character.

f23:
Professions are trade skills used to gather, craft, or enhance items, helping you earn gold and improve your character. 

They’re divided into either a Gathering Profession or a Crafting Profession and can be categorized as a limited Primary Profession, which are limited, or a Secondary Skill which is always available to learn.
f40:
Professions are trade skills your character can learn to gather, craft, or enhance items that support your progression. They offer a valuable way to earn gold, improve your gear, and contribute to your character’s development.

Each profession falls into one of two categories: a Gathering Profession or a Crafting Profession. Gathering professions encourage you to explore the world, collecting raw materials from nodes found throughout various zones. Crafting professions allow you to learn Recipes and use those raw materials, along with loot from enemies, to create powerful gear, consumables, and enhancements.

Additionally, professions fall into two categories: a Primary Profession or a Secondary Skill. Primary professions are more impactful and limited as by default, you can only learn two. Secondary skills, such as Cooking and First Aid, are available to all players with no restriction on how many you can learn.

To learn a Profession, visit a Profession Trainer or a Book of Artisans to get started.

f23:
PvE Mode is a ruleset that prevents open-world PvP, so other players cannot attack you. 

While in PvE mode, you cannot heal or assist anyone in PvP combat.
f40:
PvE Mode is a ruleset that protects players from open-world PvP combat. 

When PvE mode is enabled, other players cannot attack you, and you are also restricted from participating in PvP activities. This includes healing or assisting players who are engaged in PvP combat. This mode is ideal for players who prefer to focus on completing a quest, exploring a sub-zone, leveling their Profession, or progressing through PvE without the risk of being ambushed by enemy players.

The PVE world is shared with No-Risk PvP Mode players, meaning both groups exist in the same zones. You’ll see other players in no-risk mode, but you won’t be able to interact with them in PvP-related ways unless you change your ruleset. However, engaging a world boss will automatically switch you to No-Risk PvP Mode for the duration of the encounter. This prevents players from bypassing PvP risk during high-value content.

To enable PvE Mode, visit your Capital City and open the Hybrid Risk Menu (Hotkey H -> PvP Ruleset Tab) then select 'PvE Mode' as your active ruleset. Keep in mind that switching between PvP modes has a 15 minute cooldown, so plan your activities accordingly.

f23:
Quest Givers are NPCs who offer quests to players. 

These NPCs are marked with icons above their heads that indicate the status of a quest and upon completion, can give items, Experience, and Reputation as rewards.
f40:
Quest Givers are NPCs that offer quests to players, helping guide progression, storytelling, and rewards throughout the world. These NPCs are easily recognized by the icons that appear above their heads, which indicate the availability or status of a quest.

An exclamation mark (!) icon means a quest is being offered:

Yellow (!) indicates a new quest is available and ready to be accepted.
Blue (!) signals a repeatable quest, which can be completed multiple times.
Grey (!) shows that a quest exists, but you currently don’t meet the requirements to accept it.

A question mark (?) icon appears when interacting with quest progress:

Yellow (?) means the quest is ready to be finished, and you can collect your rewards.
Blue (?) indicates a repeatable quest that has been completed and can be turned in again.
Grey (?) shows that you’ve accepted the quest, but the objective has not been completed.

Quest givers are found throughout the world and serve as one of the main ways players gain Experience, Currency, gear, and story progression.

f23: A Raid can refer to either challenging instanced content for 10–25 players, or a large party, (called a raid group), consisting of 6 to 40 players.
f40:
Raids refer to both a specific type of group as well as a category of high-level PvE content. 

A 'raid group' is a large Party consisting of anywhere from 6 to 40 players, formed when a Party leader converts a standard group using the raid menu (Hotkey O -> Raid Tab -> Convert to Raid). 

Raid groups are typically used for content that requires more coordination and members than regular Dungeons or quests. However, it’s important to note that while in a Raid group, most normal quests won’t track progress.

The term ""raid"" also refers to raid encounters, which are instanced dungeons designed for 10 to 25 players. These encounters feature powerful bosses, complex mechanics, and often require strategic coordination, communication, and strong team builds. Raids offer some of the most prestigious rewards in the game, including high-tier gear, Mounts, cosmetic items, and unique achievements.

f23:
Talents are powerful traits that enhance abilities, modify gameplay, or unlock new tools, helping define your character’s combat style. 

In Wildcard Mode, talents are randomly rolled from any class as you level up, adding unpredictability and encouraging creative builds.
f40:
Talents are a core progression system that allow players to shape their character’s combat identity by selecting powerful traits that enhance abilities, modify gameplay, or unlock entirely new tools. 

In Wildcard Mode, a talent is not chosen manually and instead is randomly rolled each time you level up, offering a dynamic and unpredictable path to building your character.

This mode removes all class-based restrictions, giving you access to talent trees from any class in the game. 

If you’re not satisfied with a talent, you can use a Scroll of Fortune to reroll it, either to improve your current setup or pursue a completely new synergy.

f23:
Talents are powerful traits that enhance abilities, modify gameplay, or unlock new tools, helping define your character’s combat style. 

In Freepick Mode you can choose any talent from any class and are not limited by investing a Talent Essence in preliminary talent nodes.
f40:
Talents are a core progression system that allow players to shape their character’s combat identity by selecting powerful traits that enhance abilities, modify gameplay, or unlock entirely new tools. 

To access your talent trees, open the Character Advancement menu (Hotkey N) and select the class and Specialization to view each tree and its corresponding abilities. In Freepick Mode, you have the freedom to mix and match talents across all classes and specializations, regardless of their location on their talent tree, allowing for ultimate customization.

If you’re not satisfied with a chosen talent, you can use a Scroll of Talent Unlearning to refund that Talent Essence. Alternatively, you can also use a Specialization purge or class purge to reset the corresponding tree and refund your talent points.

f23:
A Recipe teaches your character how to craft a specific item within a Profession. 

Recipes can be learned from a Profession Trainer, purchased from Vendors, traded between players, or looted from enemies throughout the world.
f40:
Recipes are special items that teach your character how to craft specific items within a Profession. Once learned, a recipe permanently adds a new crafting option to your profession's crafting menu. Recipes are essential for progressing through professions and unlocking powerful gear, consumables, and utility items.

You can acquire recipes in several ways: by learning them from a Profession Trainer, purchasing them from specialized Vendors, trading with other players, or looting them from enemies. Some recipes are easy to find, while others are tied to specific Reputation milestones, quests, or Dungeons.

f23:
By clicking the (?) in the Micro Menu or visiting Ameer Greatluck in a Capital City, you can access the Recovery Services menu. 

This lets you restore items that you have recently discarded and recover deleted characters.
f40:
Recovery Services can restore items that you may have lost accidentally. Whether you’ve sold an item to a Vendor, deleted it, or disenchanted it, you can often recover it using this system. 

To access Recovery Services, click the question mark icon (?) in the micro menu, or speak with Ameer Greatluck, who can be found in most Capital Cities. This will open the recovery menu, where you'll see a list of recently lost items eligible for restoration.

You can recover up to the last 500 lost items for a fee, and also restore deleted characters through this menu. It serves as a reliable safety net for undoing mistakes or recovering important items.

f23:
At an Enchanting Altar, you can reroll Mystic Scrolls for new, random Mystic Enchants. 

Reforging costs Mystic Runes and can be done as many times as you’d like on the same scroll.
f40:
Reforging is the process of rerolling Mystic Scrolls to receive a new, random Mystic Enchant. Access the reforge menu (Hotkey N -> Mystic Enchant Tab -> Enchant Scrolls) at an Enchanting Altar to reforge.

Reforging costs Mystic Runes, a Currency used exclusively for enchant manipulation, and there is no limit to how many times you can reforge the same scroll so long as you have the resources.

If you don’t already have a mystic scroll, you can conveniently purchase one directly from the reforge menu, making it easy to start the process. Each time you reforge a scroll, you also gain Experience towards your Mystic Enchanting Level.

f23:
At an Enchanting Altar, you can reroll Mystic Scrolls for new, random Mystic Enchants. 

Reforging costs Marks of Ascension and can be done as many times as you’d like on the same scroll.

f23:
Reputation is a system that tracks your standing with various factions, progressing from hated to exalted and unlocking rewards like gear and cosmetics. 

You can gain or lose reputation through actions such as quests, combat, or setting factions to ""At War,"" which may affect your access to their services.
f40:
Reputation (Hotkey U) is a progression system that tracks your standing with various factions throughout the world. 

Each faction has its own unique identity, goals, and rewards, and building reputation with them often unlocks valuable items such as gear, Mounts, Companions, Recipes, item enhancements, and cosmetics. 

Your standing with a faction typically progresses through several ranks: hated, hostile, unfriendly, neutral, friendly, honored, revered, and finally exalted. You begin at neutral with most factions, and by completing quests, killing specific enemies, turning in items, or participating in events tied to that faction, you can steadily increase your Reputation.

Additionally, certain factions can be set to 'At War' status, allowing you to attack their NPCs. Doing so will lower your reputation, potentially pushing it into negative standings like unfriendly or hated, which can impact your ability to access quests or Vendors from that group.

f23: Resilience is a secondary stat that reduces the damage taken from other Players and their Pets in PvP combat.
f40:
Resilience is a secondary stat that reduces the damage you take from other players and their Tamed Pets in PvP combat. This makes it an important stat for increasing your survivability in battlegrounds and arenas.

You can view your resilience rating in Character Info (Hotkey C).

f23:
Resistances reduce the damage you take from specific types of magical attacks. 

The higher your resistance, the better your chance to partially or fully resist spells from that school of magic.
f40:
Resistances reduce the amount of damage you take from specific types of magical attacks. There are five primary resistance types: fire, frost, shadow, nature, and arcane.

When you are targeted by a magical spell, your resistance provides a chance to either partially resist the damage (reducing the damage taken) or fully resisting it (taking no damage at all). The effectiveness of resistances is based on your resistance rating, the level of the caster, and the difficulty of the content you're facing. 

In general gameplay, resistances are not always essential, but they become critically important in certain situations. A high-level Dungeon, Raid, or world boss can often feature encounters with heavy elemental damage where resistances can significantly improve your survivability. In PvP, resistances can provide a strong defensive edge against caster-heavy opponents, allowing you to withstand or shrug off powerful spell-based attacks.

You can find your current resistances in Character Info (Hotkey C).

f23: Rested Experience is a bonus Experience modifier earned by logging out in rest areas, doubling Experience gained from kills until depleted.
f40:
Rested Experience is a modifier that lets you level up faster by granting extra Experience points when you kill enemies. Your character accumulates rested Experience whenever you log out inside an inn or a Capital City, also known as rest areas. 

This bonus appears as a blue section on your Experience bar and effectively doubles the Experience gained from killing monsters until the rested amount is used up. However, rested Experience does not apply to quest rewards, only to kills.

f23:
Talents are powerful traits that enhance abilities, modify gameplay, or unlock new tools, helping define your character’s combat style. 

Each class has three possible talent trees, and the more Talent Essences you invest in each tree, the more powerful talents you can obtain.
f40:
Talents are a core progression system that allow players to shape their character’s combat identity by selecting powerful traits that enhance abilities, modify gameplay, or unlock entirely new tools. 

To access your talent trees, open the Character Advancement menu (Hotkey N) and select one of the three tabs at the top to view each tree and its corresponding abilities. You can mix and match talents across all three trees, allowing for deep customization. However, you must invest points in earlier nodes before unlocking talents further down the tree. The deeper you go, the more powerful the talents become.

If you’re not satisfied with a chosen talent, you can use Marks of Ascension to refund that Talent Essence. Alternatively, you can also use a talent purge to reset your talents completely and allow you to start over.

f23: Riding Trainers are NPCs found in your Capital City, and occasionally a quest hub, who can teach you how to ride Mounts and improve your riding speed.
f40:
Riding Trainers are NPCs found in your Capital City, and occasionally a quest hub, who can teach you how to ride Mounts and improve your riding speed. 

They also provide training for flying Mounts in Outland and Northrend once you reach the appropriate level and requirements. 

Riding comes in several tiers, each increasing your speed and unlocking new movement options:

Apprentice Riding – Increases ground mount speed by 60%.
Journeyman Riding – Upgrades ground mount speed to 100%.
Expert Riding – Unlocks flying at 150% flight speed.
Artisan Riding – Improves flying speed to 280%.
Extraordinary Riding – Grants the maximum flying speed of 310%.

f23: A Scroll of Retreat is a special teleportation item stored in your Vanity Collection (Hotkey N -> Vanity Tab) that instantly transports your character back to your Capital City.
f40:
A Scroll of Retreat is a special teleportation item stored in your Vanity Collection (Hotkey N -> Vanity Tab) that instantly transports your character back to your Capital City. 

Every character gets a scroll upon reaching level 20. To use it, open the Vanity Collection, select the scroll, and click 'Deliver Item' to add it to your inventory to use like any other item.

You can use a Scroll of Retreat at any level, but unlike a Hearthstone or Stones of Retreat, it has a long cooldown, so it's best to save your scroll for when you want to avoid a Flightpath or really need to fast travel.

f23: Scrolls of Fortune (SoF) are essential for Wildcard builds, allowing you to reroll spells and Talents. Silas grants free scrolls while leveling and offers additional capped scrolls for Marks of Ascension at max level.
f40: Scrolls of Fortune (SoF) are a core feature of Wildcard, where your character abilities are learned randomly rather than chosen manually. These scrolls let you reroll unwanted spells or Talents, giving you more control over your build as you level. Visit Silas Darkmoon every 10 levels to claim free Scrolls; each Specialization has its own Scroll of Fortune progress, so you do not have to choose which spec receives your leveling scrolls. At max level, Silas offers additional Scrolls of Fortune for Marks of Ascension with a claim cap, while uncapped Scrolls can be earned from Call Board Caches, Dungeons, Battlegrounds, Manastorm, Raids, High-Risk farming, and more. There are two types of scrolls: Scroll of Fortune, which can reroll an Ability or Talent, and Scroll of Fortune: Talents, which rerolls Talents only.

f23: A Secondary Skill is a Profession that every character can level and learn separate from their limited Primary Profession.
f40:
Secondary Skills are a Profession that every character can learn, regardless of their build or playstyle. Unlike a Primary Profession, which are limited by default to two per character, all heroes can learn and level every secondary skill. 

The available secondary skills are:

Cooking - Cook meat and fish to create powerful consumables. (Crafting Profession)
First Aid - Create bandages and healing items that you can use in combat. (Crafting Profession)
Fishing - Catch fish and sunken loot in any body of water. (Gathering Profession)
Woodcutting - Chop down logs and turn them into lumber for quests. (Gathering Profession)

You can train these skills by visiting a Book of Artisans or the appropriate Profession Trainer found in your Capital City or quest hub.

f23:
Primary Professions can be divided into two types, a Gathering Profession or a Crafting Profession. 

By default, you can learn up to two of these professions. To unlock more primary Profession slots, you will need a Craftsman’s Codex.
f40:
Primary Professions are the main professions your character can learn and develop. They are divided into two categories and can be a Gathering Profession or a Crafting Profession. 

By default, each character can learn up to two Primary Professions, allowing you to choose any combination that suits your playstyle.

If you want to expand beyond this limit, you can unlock additional Profession slots by obtaining a special item called the Craftsman’s Codex. This item enables you to learn and progress in more professions simultaneously, providing even greater flexibility and depth to your character’s skills. 

Managing your primary professions effectively can greatly enhance your gameplay, economy, and overall progression.

f23:
Skinning is a Primary Profession and a Gathering Profession that gathers hides, leather, and scales from beasts using a skinning knife.

Items gathered from Skinning are primarily used in the Crafting Profession Leatherworking.
f40:
Skinning is a Primary Profession and a Gathering Profession for players who enjoy exploring the open world while collecting natural resources. Leathers gathered by skinners are used in a Crafting Profession like Leatherworking.

To get started, you’ll need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn skinning. Once trained, you can begin gathering leather by fighting beasts and harvesting their hides after taking the loot. Skinning is unique to other gathering professions as it is not based on open world nodes, but rather defeated enemies.

Every time you skin a beast, you have a chance to contribute to your skinning skill and obtain leather used directly in crafting. Different beasts contain different types of hide, typically tied to level ranges and progression, so exploring new areas and defeating new enemies becomes a rewarding part of leveling the Profession.

To harvest beasts, you’ll need a skinning knife, which can be purchased from Vendors, or the Skin-Peeler 9000 to automatically skin nearby defeated beasts. This tool must be in your inventory while gathering and is essential for collecting leather. For those managing multiple professions, investing in an Ethereal Tool Dispenser can be helpful as this item consolidates all Profession tools into a single inventory slot and is available from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP) or from the Auction House for in-game gold.

f23: The Skills tab (Hotkey K) provides a detailed overview of your character’s various proficiencies like weapon skills, Profession level, and languages.
f40:
The Skills tab (Hotkey K) provides a detailed overview of your character’s various proficiencies. 

This includes your skill levels in weaponry tracks your available Armor Type, class-related abilities (like stealth or lockpicking), Profession levels (such as Blacksmithing or Herbalism), Secondary Skill level (like Cooking and First Aid), and even languages your character can understand or speak. 

As you use weapons in combat or actively work on professions, your skill levels increase naturally, improving your effectiveness with those tools or trades. For example, leveling a weapon skill makes you more accurate and efficient in combat with that weapon type, while increasing a Profession skill allows you to craft higher-level items.

f23: Spell Power (also known as SP) is a secondary stat that increases the damage and healing of spells.
f40:
Spell Power (also known as SP) is a secondary stat that increases the damage and healing done by your spells. A higher spell power value means your magical abilities will hit harder or restore more health, making it essential for both casters and hybrid builds.

You can view your spell power in Character Info (Hotkey C).

f23:
The Spellbook (Hotkey P) displays all the spells, abilities, and passives your character has learned. 

You can drag spells from the spellbook onto your action bars for quick access during combat.
f40:
The Spellbook (Hotkey P) is where you can view and manage all the spells, abilities, and passives your character has learned. 

It’s divided into several tabs for easy organization:

Class Tabs - Contains spells and attacks organized by class
General Tab - Contains racial abilities, passive effects and professions
Vanity Tab - Contains vanity spells and cosmetics
Ascension Manastorm Item Tab - Contains Manastorm Spells and Items

You can drag abilities from any of these tabs directly onto your action bars for quick use in combat or exploration.

f23:
Spirit is the Primary Attribute for those who dedicate themselves to healing and support. 

It empowers healers by increasing their Healing Power and granting access to unique restorative spells.
f40:
Spirit is the Primary Attribute that represents regenerative power. Spirit is essential for characters who rely on mana as it primarily boosts your mana regeneration rate, especially while out of combat or when using abilities that allow regeneration during casting. It can also increase health regeneration, which benefits classes or builds that value endurance and passive healing over time.

Effects of spirit:

Increases Mana Regeneration, particularly out of combat.
Improves health regeneration when not actively taking damage.
When paired with certain Talents or abilities, it can contribute to Mana Regeneration during combat.
Some healing effects scale with spirit in certain builds.

f23:
Stamina is a Primary Attribute available to all players. 

It represents your character’s overall toughness and endurance, directly increasing your total health pool.
f40:
Stamina is the Primary Attribute that represents physical endurance, toughness, and overall survivability. It directly increases your maximum health, making it the cornerstone stat for any character that expects to take damage.

Stamina is especially important for Tanks, but it's useful for every class and role, as more health always means a greater chance of surviving mistakes, burst damage, or unavoidable mechanics.

Effects of Stamina:
+1 Stamina increases maximum health by 10.
In some builds or Talents, stamina may also improve Resistances, healing received, or threat generation.

f23: A Stone of Retreat lets you instantly teleport to cities and major quest hubs across the world.
f40:
Stones of Retreat are convenient teleportation items that allow you to instantly travel to major cities and quest hubs throughout the open world. 

Once acquired, a stone of retreat is added to your Vanity Collection, and after learning it, you can use it at any time either from your Spellbook or by shift-clicking the destination directly on your World Map. These stones make traveling much faster and are especially useful for skipping long flight paths or returning to key locations quickly. 

Stones of Retreat can be obtained from the Auction House or Tiraxis for in-game Currency, alternatively they can be purchased from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

f23:
Stony Tark, located in any Capital City or Starter Zone, lets players access the Trials menu (Hotkey J) to begin unique challenges starting at level 1. 

Trials can be viewed anytime with the menu, but new ones must be started by speaking with Stony Tark.
f40:
Stony Tark is an NPC who gives players access to the Trials menu (Hotkey J), a feature that allows you to take on optional leveling challenges with unique rules and rewards. 

You can find Stony Tark in any Capital City or starter zone. To begin a trial, your character must be level 1 as either a freshly created character or one that has just been Prestiged. 

Interacting with Stony Tark opens the Trials menu, where you can choose from a variety of Trials that may limit gear, abilities, or add permadeath mechanics. While you can view the rules of your trial at any time through the Trials menu, starting or ending a new one always requires speaking with Stony Tark in person.

f23: Stormwind (SW) is the last human kingdom and serves as the Capital City for the Alliance in Elwynn Forest.
f40:
Stormwind (SW) is the last remaining human kingdom in the world of Azeroth and serves as the majestic Capital City of the Alliance faction. Located in the peaceful region of Elwynn Forest, Stormwind is a bustling hub where players of the Alliance can find important NPCs, Vendors, Class Trainers, and Quest Givers.

As the heart of human civilization, Stormwind is known for its towering stone walls, grand architecture, and iconic structures such as the Cathedral of Light and the Stormwind Keep, home to King Varian Wrynn. 

The city is divided into several districts, each with its own purpose like the Trade District hosting Bank and Auction House, the Mage Quarter for magical training, and the Dwarven District where you can find access to the Deeprun Tram.

It is a safe haven from monsters and enemy players, making it an ideal place to rest, craft, trade, and prepare for adventures throughout Azeroth.

f23:
Strength is the Primary Attribute that embodies raw physical power. 

It's ideal for players who want to play a bruiser-style character that’s capable of taking hits and dealing out massive melee damage.
f40:
Strength is the Primary Attribute that represents raw physical power and brute force. It is a key stat for players who want to excel in close-quarters combat, particularly with melee weapons like swords, axes, and maces. Strength increases your Attack Power, which directly boosts the amount of damage your character can deal with physical melee abilities and auto-attacks.

Effects of Strength:

+1 Strength typically increases Melee Attack Power by 2.

f23:
Soulbound items are permanently bound to a character, preventing trade or sale with other players. 

There are two types of soulbinding: bind on equip (bound when worn) and bind on pickup (bound immediately).
f40:
Soulbound items are objects that become permanently bound to a single character, preventing them from being traded, mailed, or sold to other players once used or equipped. This system ensures that powerful equipment remains unique to the player who earned or looted it. Most high-level gear obtained from a Dungeon, Raid, and certain quests are Soulbound.

There are two primary types of soulbinding:

Bind on Equip (BoE): These items become soulbound the moment you equip them for the first time. Until equipped, BoE items can be freely traded or sold to other players.

Bind on Pickup (BoP): These items become soulbound immediately upon looting or receiving them, making them untradeable from the start.

While soulbinding is generally permanent, some equipment can become Bloodforged, which converts the item into a special version of PvP gear that is tradeable.

f23: Silas Darkmoon is a key Wildcard NPC who grants Scrolls of Fortune while leveling, offers max-level Scrolls for Marks of Ascension, sells Skill Card Packs, and accepts Darkmoon Tickets for rewards.
f40: Silas Darkmoon is a key Wildcard NPC found in Capital Cities and early quest hubs. As you level, Silas offers free Scrolls of Fortune every 10 levels so you can reroll unwanted spells or Talents and shape your build. At max level, Silas offers additional capped Scrolls of Fortune for Marks of Ascension, and you can earn more Scrolls through end-game content. Silas also grants Sealed Card Packs from max-level Scroll of Fortune quests; these packs reveal max-level Talent Skill Cards that are added to your account-wide Skill Card Collection. Darkmoon Tickets from Card Packs can be redeemed with Silas for specific Skill Cards, random uncollected cards, cosmetic prizes, and other Wildcard rewards.

f23:
Tailoring is a Primary Profession and a Crafting Profession that focuses on transforming cloth materials into gear, Bags, and powerful spellthreads.

Tailoring uses cloth dropped from humanoid enemies for materials.
f40:
Tailoring is a Primary Profession and a Crafting Profession focused on transforming cloth materials found throughout the world into a wide range of items such as equipment, item enhancements, large Bags to expand your inventory, and even Mounts.

To begin, you’ll need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn tailoring. Once trained, you can start collecting or purchasing the required materials. Tailoring relies primarily on cloth dropped from humanoid enemies across the open world and turning them into larger bolts of material.

As you level up, you'll unlock Recipes, known as patterns, that teach you how to craft specific armor pieces, Bags, and spell-enhancing items. In addition to wearable gear, tailors can also craft spellthreads that can be applied to equipment to boost stats and are particularly useful for caster builds.

While tailors do not require a special tool to sew their patterns, many players combine it with other professions like Enchanting to streamline their material supply. For those managing multiple professions, investing in an Ethereal Tool Dispenser can be helpful as this item consolidates all Profession tools into a single inventory slot and is available from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP) or from the Auction House for in-game gold.

f23:
Stamina is a Primary Attribute available to all players. 

It represents your character’s overall toughness and endurance, directly increasing your total health pool.
f40:
Stamina is a vital Primary Attribute available to all players, regardless of their chosen path. It represents your character’s overall toughness and endurance, directly increasing your total health pool. Stamina is especially important for Tank players, who rely on a large health pool to absorb damage and protect their allies.

Unlike other primary attributes, stamina does not have a dedicated path or passive bonuses but remains an essential stat for anyone looking to improve their survivability in combat.

f23:
Talents are powerful traits that enhance abilities, modify gameplay, or unlock new tools, helping define your character’s combat style. 

Each Specialization has its own talent tree and class tree that require you to invest points in earlier nodes before progressing deeper to the most powerful talents.
f40:
Talents are a core progression system that allow players to shape their character’s combat identity by selecting powerful traits that enhance abilities, modify gameplay, or unlock entirely new tools. 

To access your talent trees, open the Character Advancement menu (Hotkey N) and after selecting your Specialization, you can view your class tree and your specialization’s talent tree. Talent trees are structured in a web-like path, requiring you to invest points in earlier nodes before progressing deeper. The deeper you go, the more powerful the talents become, encouraging thoughtful planning as you advance through the tree.

If you’re not satisfied with a chosen talent, you can use Marks of Ascension to refund that Talent Essence. Alternatively, you can also use a specialization purge or class purge to reset the corresponding tree and refund your talent points.

f23:
Tamed pets are combat pets that aid you in battle with unique abilities, and some offer customizable Pet Talents. 

There are many different types of pets including beasts, demons, dragonkin, elementals, demons, and undead.
f40:
Tamed pets are creatures that assist you in battle, each offering unique abilities based on their type. Some pets even come with Pet Talents, allowing you to customize their skills and playstyle to fit your combat needs. You can view the stats and details of your tamed pet in the Pets Tab (Hotkey Shift + P).

You can only have one tamed pet active at a time, but there are many types to choose from, including beasts, demons, undead, dragonkin, and elementals. Summoning a pet depends on its classification and requires specific spells: Tame Beast, Tame Dragonkin, Tether Elemental, Summon Demon, Enslave Demon, and Dominate Undead. 

There are two ways to acquire combat pets: by finding and taming them directly in the open world, or by using a Realm-Bound item known as a pet whistle. Each whistle is tied to a specific pet and can be found in the Wardrobe (Hotkey N -> Wardrobe Tab -> Pets). These whistles can drop from their corresponding creatures in the world, be purchased from the Auction House, or obtained from the Ascension Store using Donation Points (DP).

Pets tamed in the open world must be managed through a stablemaster if you wish to swap between them. However, pets acquired via whistles are far more convenient, allowing you to switch your active pet anytime and anywhere without needing to visit a stable.

f23:
A Tank specializes in absorbing damage and keeping enemies focused on themselves to protect their group. 

Using defensive skills and threat management, tanks ensure teammates stay safe, making them essential in PvE content.
f40:
A Tank is a player who specializes in absorbing damage and serving as the primary protector of their group by maintaining enemy focus on themselves. 

Tanks utilize a combination of defensive abilities, threat management, and crowd control to mitigate incoming damage and control the flow of combat. By drawing enemy aggression (aggro) away from more vulnerable teammates, tanks create safe opportunities for damage dealers and healers to perform their roles effectively.

f23: Tiraxis is an NPC near the Auction House who runs several specialty shops like the Ethereal Bazaar, selling unique cosmetics and consumable Donation Items for Bazaar Tokens.
f40:
Tiraxis is an NPC located near the Auction House in your Capital City, serving as the host of several specialty shops. 

Among these is the highly sought-after Ethereal Bazaar, offering a wide selection of unique and valuable items. Tiraxis also sells essential goods such as Heirlooms, Stones of Retreat for quick teleportation, Titan Scrolls that grant powerful realm-wide buffs, keeper scrolls to aid your professions and leveling journey, and the Ethereal Box of Wares containing retired seasonal items and random miscellaneous goods from the Ethereal Bazaar. 

All purchases from Tiraxis require Bazaar Tokens which can be bought from the Auction House or through the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

f23:
Titan Scrolls are consumables that provide powerful realm-wide buffs, stacking up to five times and benefiting all players outside starter zones. 

Each scroll offers unique effects and can be acquired through drops, vendors, the Auction House, or the Ascension Store.
f40:
Titan Scrolls are powerful consumable items that provide realm-wide buffs, benefiting every player in the open world, except for those in starter zones. Each type of scroll can stack up to 5 times, and all five different scrolls can be active simultaneously, combining their effects for maximum benefit.

The five Titan Scrolls and their effects are:

Norgannon: Increases damage dealt to enemies and boosts experience gained from combat.
Eonar: Can create a ring of flowers upon defeating an enemy, restoring health and mana.
Aggramar: Increases damage dealt to demons.
Khaz’goroth: Boosts Experience gained from a Profession.
Golganneth: Enhances swim speed and grants underwater breathing.

Titan Scrolls can be discovered as drops throughout the world, purchased from Vendors or the Auction House using in-game Currency, or bought from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

f23:
Spirit is the Primary Attribute for those who dedicate themselves to healing and support. 

It empowers healers by increasing their Healing Power and granting access to unique restorative spells.
f40:
Spirit is the Primary Attribute for those who dedicate themselves to healing and support. It empowers healers by increasing their Healing Power and granting access to unique restorative spells. Spirit is essential for players who want to keep their allies alive and turn the tide of battle through powerful healing.

Choosing the Path of Mending makes spirit your main stat, greatly enhancing your healing. 

You gain bonus Healing Power, Intellect, and spirit, boosting both your spell effectiveness and resource regeneration. Additionally, every point of Spell Power also increases your Healing Power, amplifying the potency of your restorative magic.

The Path of Mending also grants two powerful passive abilities, depending on your weapon choice:

Spiritual Acceleration: When wielding a two-handed weapon, your Spell Haste is increased by 10% and your Spell Critical Strike Chance is increased by 3%, allowing you to cast healing spells faster and with greater impact.

Empowered Mending: When using a one-handed weapon, your healing is increased by 5%, making every heal more effective and helping keep your party alive.

f23:
Transmogrification lets you change your gear’s appearance using collected looks without affecting stats or performance. 

Appearances unlock automatically when you equip items, allowing you to customize your character’s style freely.
f40:
Transmogrification (commonly called 'transmog' or 'mog') is a cosmetic system that allows you to change the appearance of your equipped gear using appearances you’ve collected in your Wardrobe (Hotkey N -> Wardrobe Tab).

This feature lets you customize your character’s look without affecting the gear’s stats or performance.

When you transmog an item, only its visual appearance changes, its stats, item level, and effects remain exactly the same. This means you can maintain your optimal gear setup while expressing your personal style or recreating iconic looks from across the game.

To unlock appearances for your Wardrobe, simply obtain the items themselves (whether through quest rewards, drops, crafting, or purchases) and they will automatically be added to your collection when you equip them.

f23:
Agility is the Primary Attribute for those who rely on speed, precision, and deadly efficiency. 

It’s ideal for players who prefer fast-paced combat, weaving together rapid attacks, critical strikes, and nimble movement.
f40:
Agility is the Primary Attribute for those who rely on speed, precision, and deadly efficiency. It’s ideal for players who prefer fast-paced combat, weaving together rapid attacks, critical strikes, and nimble movement. Agility is especially beneficial for leather and mail Armor Type users who favor mobility over brute force or spellcasting.

Effects of Agility:

+1 Agility increases Ranged Attack Power by 1-2 (depending on class).
+1 Agility increases Melee Attack Power by 1-2 (depending on class).
+1 Agility increases Armor by 1 (while wearing mail or leather).
Increases Critical Strike Chance with both melee and ranged attacks.
Increases Dodge Rating, making you harder to hit in close combat.

f23:
Trials are self-imposed challenges that add unique modifiers to leveling, offering exclusive rewards, cosmetics, and achievements for completing the leveling journey under special conditions. 

They must be started at level 1 through Stony Tark and can be viewed anytime via the trials menu (Hotkey J).
f40:
Trials are special self-imposed challenges that add unique twists to the leveling journey. They reward creativity, skill, and dedication by offering exclusive rewards, cosmetics, and achievements for completing the game under specific conditions.

You can view active trials at any time through the trials menu (Hotkey J), but trials can only be initiated or deactivated by speaking with Stony Tark, found in any Capital City or starter zone. To begin a trial, your character must be level 1, either as a brand-new character or immediately after prestiging.

Each trial imposes different restrictions or gameplay modifiers (such as permadeath, changing the ways you obtain Experience, or adding in completely new challenges) that make the leveling process more difficult and rewarding.

f23:
A Tome of Specialization unlocks extra Specialization slots, letting you save and switch between full build loadouts like PvE, PvP, or tanking. 

Up to seven slots use standard tomes, while a Master’s Tome is required for the eighth and beyond.
f40:
A Tome of Specialization allows you to unlock additional Specialization slots on your character, giving you the flexibility to create and save multiple unique builds.

Each tome unlocks a specific Specialization slot, and slots must be unlocked in order starting with your second Specialization. Your second slot's tome can be purchased directly from Nozdormu using in-game Currency. Additional slots, up to the seventh, can be unlocked using these numbered tomes, which are available from the Auction House, Tiraxis, or the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

To unlock your eighth slot and beyond, you’ll need a Master’s Tome of Specialization.

Once unlocked, each Specialization slot lets you swap between character loadouts without having to manually reset or rebuild your character. This makes it easy to switch between PvE and PvP builds, Tanking and DPS, all on the same character.

f23:
Specializations (specs) enhance your class and grant unique abilities that help define your character’s role and theme. 

With a Tome of Specialization, you can unlock and switch between multiple builds on the same character.
f40:
Specializations (or specs) grant unique abilities that help define your character’s role (Tank, Healer, or DPS) and theme.

You can choose your specialization upon reaching level 10 in Character Advancement (Hotkey N). Once chosen, a Primary Attribute will be recommended to you and your class and specialization talent trees will be unlocked.

With a Tome of Specialization, you can unlock multiple specialization loadouts, giving you the flexibility to create and swap between different specs and talent builds on the same character.

f23:
Strength is the Primary Attribute that embodies raw physical power. 

It's ideal for players who want to play a bruiser-style character that’s capable of taking hits and dealing out massive melee damage.
f40:
Strength is the Primary Attribute that represents raw physical power and brute force. It is a key stat for players who want to excel in close-quarters combat, particularly with melee weapons like swords, axes, and maces. Strength increases your Attack Power, which directly boosts the amount of damage your character can deal with physical melee abilities and auto-attacks.

Effects of Strength:

+1 Strength typically increases Melee Attack Power by 2.
+2 Strength typically increases Block Value by 1.

f23:
The Vanity Collection sync keeps your cosmetic collection unified across all live Ascension realms, automatically sharing any collection item between worlds. 

It updates on login and is available from Tiraxis, the Auction House, or the Ascension Store.
f40:
The Vanity Collection sync is a powerful item that keeps your cosmetic collection unified across all live Ascension realms (excluding PTR servers). It ensures that any Realm-Bound Mounts, Companions, appearances, toys, Heirlooms, or non-consumable Donation Items you've unlocked on one realm are available on other servers.

Each time you log in, the Vanity Collection sync automatically updates your collection, merging cosmetic data between realms.

You can obtain the Vanity Collection sync from Tiraxis as well as the Auction House with in-game Currency, or you can purchase it from the Ascension Store with Donation Points (DP).

f23: The Vanity Collection (Hotkey N -> Vanity Tab) is your menu for managing all of your Realm-Bound items.
f40:
The Vanity Collection (Hotkey N -> Vanity Tab) is your menu for managing all of your Realm-Bound items. This includes Mounts, Tamed Pet appearances, toys, equipment cosmetics, Companions, Heirlooms, and non-consumable Donation Items. 

All items in your Vanity Collection are shared across all characters on the same realm, allowing you to easily access your favorite items regardless of which character you're playing.

You can instantly deliver any item from your collection to any of your characters at any time. This makes it incredibly convenient to equip cosmetics or toys without needing to transfer items manually.

If you play on multiple live realms, you can use a Vanity Collection Sync to copy your unlocked cosmetics across realms, ensuring your collection stays consistent no matter where you play.

The Vanity tab is also where the seasonal shop can be browsed, offering access to exclusive appearances, pets, and other themed rewards during the current realm’s season.

f23: Vendors are NPCs found throughout the world who sell a wide variety of items and can also purchase your unwanted goods, helping you manage your inventory more efficiently.
f40:
Vendors are NPCs who sell a wide variety of useful items such as weapons, armor, consumables, and crafting materials. They also buy items from you, helping you manage your inventory by turning unwanted loot into gold. If you accidentally sell something important, vendors offer a buyback tab that lets you repurchase recently sold items. 

Vendors come in different types such as general goods vendors, trade suppliers, reagents vendors, or weapon and armor merchants. Some of these NPCs provide repair services to restore your equipment’s Durability. 

Vendors can be found in towns, cities, and quest hubs or just walking down the road all throughout the open world. If you need a specific type of vendor, the Map Lens offers a variety of search options to highlight the NPC you need.

f23:

It's ideal for players who want to play a bruiser-style character that’s capable of taking hits and dealing out massive melee damage.
f40:
Strength is the Primary Attribute that embodies raw physical power. It's ideal for players who want to play a bruiser-style character that’s capable of taking hits and dealing out massive melee damage.

Choosing the Path of Might makes strength your main stat, turning it into a key part of both your offense and defense. Each point of strength increases your Attack Power and improves your Parry chance, making you more effective in both dealing and withstanding damage on the front lines.

The Path of Might also grants two powerful passive abilities, depending on your weapon choice:

Devastating Strikes: Increases your Armor Penetration by 20% when wielding a one-handed weapon, allowing you to cut through enemy defenses more easily.

Heavy Swings: Boosts your physical and ranged ability damage by 10% when using a two-handed weapon, delivering devastating blows that can shift the tide of battle.

f23:
The Wardrobe (Hotkey N) lets you manage and customize your character’s appearance by applying collected gear looks without affecting stats. 

You can Transmogrify your gear, save custom outfits, and easily switch styles for any occasion, combining fashion with function.
f40:
The Wardrobe (Hotkey N -> Wardrobe Tab) is your central hub for managing the cosmetic appearance of your character. Through the wardrobe, you can view all the equipment appearances you’ve collected over time, including individual armor pieces, incarnations, spell cosmetics, and complete full gear sets. This system lets you customize your look without sacrificing the stats or functionality of your equipped gear.

One of the wardrobe’s key features is the ability to Transmogrify (or mog) the appearance of your current gear to match any collected visuals, giving you full control over your character’s style. Beyond simple transmogging, the wardrobe allows you to create and save custom outfits, making it easy to switch between different looks instantly.

f23: Wildcard Mode randomly assigns your spells, abilities, and Talents as you level, creating a constantly changing playstyle. Scrolls of Fortune and Skill Cards give you ways to influence the build you roll.
f40: Wildcard Mode offers a unique and unpredictable adventure where your character spells, abilities, and Talents are randomly assigned as you level. This creates a constantly shifting playstyle that tests your adaptability and creativity. To help influence your build despite the unpredictability, you can use Scrolls of Fortune to reroll unwanted spells and Talents. You can also collect Skill Cards and activate them early in a build to guarantee specific spells or Talents when they become available. Skill Card collections are shared across your account, so new characters and Prestiged characters can benefit from cards you have already collected.

f23:
Woodcutting is a Secondary Skill and a Gathering Profession that gathers wood from tree nodes using a Lumber Axe.

Items gathered from Woodcutting are currently used to complete the Call Board Daily Quests.
f40:
Woodcutting is a Secondary Skill, similar to a Gathering Profession, for players who enjoy exploring the open world while collecting natural resources. Lumber gathered by woodcutters is used to complete quests and serves as an exploration-focused activity.

To get started, you’ll need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn woodcutting. Once trained, you can begin gathering by locating and chopping down tree nodes found throughout the open world. After learning the skill, you’ll also unlock the 'Find Trees' function in the Map Lens, which highlights nearby tree nodes, making it much easier to spot gathering opportunities as you explore.

Each log you gather can boost your woodcutting skill and yields wood materials for quest objectives. Different zones feature trees tied to level ranges, making exploration key to progression. Logs can be refined into lumber at sawmills for extra skill points. Though lumber isn't used in crafting yet, it's often needed for the Call Board Daily Quest.

To harvest trees, you’ll need a lumber axe, which can be purchased from Vendors. This tool must be in your inventory while gathering and is essential for collecting logs. For those managing multiple professions, investing in an Ethereal Tool Dispenser can be helpful as this item consolidates all Profession tools into a single inventory slot and is available from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP) or from the Auction House for in-game gold.

f23:
The World Map (Hotkey M) helps you navigate Azeroth by showing your current location and zone. 

You can zoom in and out to explore continents, with each Sub-Zone revealing more detail as it's discovered.
f40:
The World Map (Hotkey M) helps you navigate Azeroth by displaying your current location and surrounding zones. 

You can zoom in and out (with Left or Right Click) to view entire continents or focus on a specific Sub-Zone. 

The map starts out mostly blank, with details only appearing as you explore the world. As you discover new areas, the map gradually fills in with terrain, labels, and points of interest, encouraging exploration and rewarding curiosity.

Important icons mark quest hubs, various Flightpath, cities, Dungeon entrances, and more. Tracked quests and objectives are also displayed directly on the map, making it easy to chart your path and find your next destination. These options are all toggleable with the magnifying glass icon in the top right corner so you can have as much, or as little information on your map as you like.

With a Tome of Specialization, you can unlock and switch between multiple builds on the same character.
f40:
Specializations (or Spec) are the three talent trees that can grant unique abilities to help define your character’s role (Tank, Healer, or DPS) and theme.

You can invest a Talent Essence in any specialization of your choice upon reaching level 10 in Character Advancement (Hotkey N). You can spend your essences in any of the three specialization trees but the most powerful Talents are at the bottom which require investment in earlier nodes to unlock.

With a Tome of Specialization, you can unlock multiple specialization loadouts, giving you the flexibility to create and swap between different builds on the same character.

f23:
Enchanting is a Primary Profession and a Crafting Profession that enhances equipment with magical effects, granting additional stats and unique bonuses.

Enchanting relies on disenchanting uncommon, rare, or epic quality gear into crafting materials but destroys the item in the process.
f40:
Enchanting is a Primary Profession and a Crafting Profession that enhances weapons and armor with magical effects to improve combat performance.

To begin, you’ll need to visit a Profession Trainer or use a Book of Artisans to learn enchanting. Once you've trained the skill, you can start collecting materials by disenchanting equipment of uncommon, rare, or epic quality. This process destroys the item, converting it into materials like dusts, essences, and shards, which are used to create enchantments. 

As you progress, you'll unlock Recipes, called formulas, that let you apply specific enchantments to gear.

Enchanting your own gear only uses materials, but selling or storing enchantments requires Enchanting Vellum from Vendors. To avoid vellum costs, use the Trade window to enchant other players’ gear, including Soulbound items.

To perform enchantments, you’ll need to craft a rod. Higher-level enchantments require more advanced rods, so it’s important to upgrade your skill tools as you progress. For those managing multiple professions, investing in an Ethereal Tool Dispenser can be helpful as this item consolidates all Profession tools into a single inventory slot and is available from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP) or from the Auction House for in-game gold.
